He has also shown that he can be left for a few hours with other dogs and settles well in their company. He will need to be fed separately, as he is a very polite little boy who would happily let another dog eat his dinner!

He can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who understand he needs time to settle in. His adopters will need to have ex-breeding experience and experience with the breed to better understand his needs.

Sheamy has been neutered and had 19 teeth removed at the time of his neutering.

With kindness, patience and the support of a friendly canine companion, we hope Sheamy will continue to grow in confidence and discover how wonderful life in a loving home can be.

Sheamy has been given the Gift of Life by Adam Culech

Sheamy has been making some lovely progress in foster and is starting to find his feet in a home environment. He is still a nervous little boy and can struggle if you try to take him out of his safe space, although he will allow himself to be picked up and cuddled and does settle once he feels secure. He is now happily coming out of his crate to wander around the house with the other dogs and has discovered that the sofa in the busiest room is a rather lovely place to be! He is quite happy to stay there even when everyone else leaves the room, although he will need a little help getting back down.Sheamy shares his space with Erin, a lovely confident Cocker Spaniel, and despite living with around 10 dogs, he has quickly shown just how much he relies on having a confident dog around him. He is also becoming more confident following the others downstairs and going out into the garden with them, although his housetraining is still a work in progress.He is still nervous when approached for a fuss but will allow gentle handling and is happy to be picked up. He will also let his foster mum put his harness on, although he does freeze when being picked up for this. Interestingly, he has discovered that he quite enjoys travelling in the dog pram while the other dogs go out for their walks!Sheamy has also shown that he can be left with the other dogs for a few hours, settling well and choosing to stay with them rather than retreating to his crate. He is a very sweet little boy who will need a kind, confident resident dog to help him continue building his confidence. Due to his small size, he would be best suited to living with a dog no bigger than a Cocker Spaniel, as larger dogs could accidentally overwhelm or knock him. He will also need to be fed separately, as he is very polite and would happily let another dog help themselves to his dinner!He is making lovely little steps forward and will need a patient home that can give him the time and reassurance he needs to keep blossoming.

Sheamy is a shy boy who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. He is a timid little chap who allows us to approach him for a gentle fuss, although he is not yet confident enough to come over to us himself. He is much livelier when he is with his kennel friends, and it is lovely to see him feeling more comfortable in their company.

Sheamy gets on wonderfully with his kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so he will need a kind resident dog in his new home, ideally a female, to help guide him and give him the reassurance he needs as he settles in and finds his paws.

As Sheamy has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. His new family will need to be patient and understanding, allowing him the time he needs to build his confidence and adjust to his new surroundings.

He can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who understand he needs time to settle in. His adopters will need to have ex-breeding experience, and experience with the breed to better understand his needs.

With kindness, patience and the support of a friendly canine companion, we hope Sheamy will gradually discover how wonderful life in a loving home can be.

description:

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I have never been on walks, but may be too scared and will need some time.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed! Read below for more info!

08-11-26 Amy is a worried but very sweet lady who has come to us from a breeder. She is quite overwhelmed to find herself here but is starting to come out of her shell more each day. Once she gets to know you, she is happy to accept a gentle fuss and we hope to see her confidence continue to grow.

name: Tiny Tim
description:
I can live with older dog-savvy children who understand I need time to settle in.

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I have never met cats.

I would love a garden to run and play in!

I would love plenty of adventures once I am fully vaccinated!

I am just a puppy! Please be patient with me while I learn the basics!

Please read below for more information about my health!

03-11-26 Tiny Tim is a gorgeous and bouncy little pup who has come to us from a breeder. He is a lovely, happy boy who is always interested in what is going on around him and has been enjoying all the new experiences that come with living in a home. He has been spending time in a foster home and is showing us what a wonderful little companion he can be. He is a fairly chilled-out little chap who loves nothing more than a cuddle, a tummy rub and being close to his favourite people!

Tiny Tim has arrived with a Grade 3 left luxating patella and a Grade 4 right luxating patella. He has had X-rays which we are able to send to potential adopters for them to have checked at their own vets. Due to his diagnosis, he will need specialist surgery to help his mobility. Unfortunately, this cannot be carried out just yet as he is still growing, and it will need to be arranged once his growth plates have fused.

We would love to find adopters who are happy to welcome Tiny Tim into their lives as he is now and who would be able to fund his operation when he is old enough. It is estimated that this could cost around £3,000+, depending on which specialist is used, and it would not be covered by insurance as it is a pre-existing condition. We would love for him to settle into a forever home while he is still a puppy, where he can enjoy all the fun of growing up with his own family. If he isn't adopted during this time, we will continue to support him and arrange his surgery under our care once he is old enough.

Tiny Tim has been enjoying life in his foster home and has shown himself to be a lovely little house companion. He is quite happy pottering about, having little naps in his bed and keeping himself occupied with his toys, although he much prefers being curled up beside his foster mum and having his tummy rubbed! He loves attention and is very generous with his kisses, even if he has been told his breath could do with a little improvement! He is also quite the little snorer and has earned himself the nickname of an 'iPad kid' because he loves sitting peacefully watching things move on a screen.

He is currently living with another dog and enjoys having company, although he can sometimes find a bigger, more playful dog a little overwhelming. He is happy to retreat to his foster mum for reassurance when he needs a break. Tiny Tim can live with a suitable resident dog in his new home, provided they are happy to have a playful puppy around, or he could be the only dog where his adopters have plenty of time to spend with him. He can live with sensible, dog-savvy children who understand his needs.

Tiny Tim has been getting out and about for some short lead walks and is slowly getting used to wearing his harness. His back legs can be a little wobbly and his mobility does need to be considered, but this certainly doesn't stop him from enjoying life! He can be quite adventurous and sometimes forgets that his legs need a little extra care, so his adopters will need to be mindful of this and manage his activity carefully. He isn't particularly keen on travelling in the car as it can make him feel sick, and loud noises can worry him, so he will need some gentle reassurance with these things.

As Tiny Tim is still just a pup, he will need to continue learning all about the rules of home life, including house training and walking nicely on a lead. His adopters will need to be patient and willing to help him grow into a happy and confident little boy. His adopters will need to agree to have him neutered when he is old enough, and his family will need to take him to puppy socialisation and training as he grows.

Tiny Tim is such a gorgeous little character who has already experienced so many firsts and is thoroughly enjoying discovering the world around him. He is a loving, cuddly and sometimes cheeky little boy who deserves a family who will adore him, understand his medical needs and be there for him throughout his journey.

Day 39 of living in a foster home with Holly, home with Holly in the evenings and socialising with humans and other doggies during the days! As cool as that is I’m sure I’d love to have a home to call my own. I have been told I’m a chill dude, I nap and cuddle and show everyone my belly for fuss, I don’t like the car it makes me sick and loud noises scare me, but Holly keeps me safe and feeds me a lot. I have a room mate, she’s a lot bigger than me and sometimes squashes me when I try to play, but Holly is always there so I run to cuddle her when it gets too much. She likes to keep me safe in my crate when she has to leave the room but I miss her a lot so I break out, I hope my new home can keep up with my magic tricks because I’ve gotten quite good at it. When Holly is busy doing human things around the home I nap in my bed keeping myself out of trouble, I nibble my toys occasionally but I much prefer pulling on Hollys hair when I get the chance. I stay close to Holly but will keep out of the way and watch from a distance if she’s having zoomies in the kitchen.

I have been told my breath stinks but that doesn’t stop me giving everyone kisses and that I snore. But Holly won’t complain because I’m the quietest boy she’s ever met. We have been out exploring every now and then, I have to wear this suit…I think it’s called a harness? I don’t like it but if it means I get to spend more time with the humans let’s go! We have done some lead walks but only short ones, I’ve got wobbly back legs so sometimes they slow me down but not by a lot. I have beds scattered around the home but I take every opportunity to lay next to Holly even on her lap for some tummy rubs. I love it! I get carried around like a baby sometimes because it means I get more tummy rubs.

Holly has called me an ‘iPad kid’ it started when we’d watch things moving on a screen and I’d sit peacefully watching it move.

Holly took me to a new vet, they put me in this big box for an X-ray. I behaved myself and watched all the other people and doggies moving around the vets from the comfort of Hollys lap (my favourite place) don’t be fooled by my wobbly legs, I forget about them a lot and try to jump up and down off the furniture, I get zoomies like any other dog, I’m curious and maybe one day my legs will not be noticed, I’ve had a few first at the rescue I even had my first Halloween at the rescue with Holly and friends and met some new friends!

Holly’s hope for me is a loving home not just for Christmas but for all the care I need, and the promise that loving me will be the greatest gift you’ll ever receive

Tiny Tim is a gorgeous and bouncy little pup who has come to us from a breeder. He is a lovely, happy boy who is always ready to see what is going on around him and would make a wonderful addition to a loving and happy family who are ready to welcome him with open arms.

Tiny Tim has arrived with a Grade 3 left luxating patella, and a Grade 4 right luxating patella. He has had x-rays which we are able to send to potential adopters for them to have checked at their own vets. Due to the diagnosis, he will need to undergo specialist surgery to help his mobility. Unfortunately, this surgery cannot be carried out at the moment as he is so young and it will need to be done once he is older as soon as his growth plates have fused.

We would love to find adopters who are happy to welcome Tiny Tim into their lives as he is now and who would be able to fund his operation when he is old enough. It's estimated that it would cost around £3000+ depending on which specialist you use and would not be covered by insurance as it's a pre-existing condition. It would be wonderful for him to settle into a loving forever home while he is still a puppy, so he can enjoy all the joys of puppyhood and get to know his new family. If he isn’t adopted during this time, we will continue to support him and arrange the surgery under our care once he is old enough.

Tiny Tim can live with a resident dog in his new home, provided they don't mind having this playful little guy around. He could also be the only dog in a home where his adopters have plenty of time to spend with him and help him learn all about life in a home. As Tiny Tim is still just a pup, he will need to learn all of the house rules, including house training and walking nicely on a lead, so his new family will need to be patient and willing to help him learn.

His adopters will also need to agree to have him neutered when he is old enough and take him to plenty of puppy socialisation and training classes. These will be really important in helping Tiny Tim grow into a happy, confident and well-rounded adult.

Tiny Tim is a gorgeous little boy with lots of fun and love to give, and he is now ready to start his journey into the wonderful world of being someone's much-loved pet!

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Sixpence
description:
I will need an adult only home, that will let me settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I can be a little nervous, and will need a secure garden to learn about the outdoors.

I have never been on walks, but may be too scared and will need some time.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

Sixpence is a nervous girl who has come to us from a breeder. She isn’t brave enough to approach you just yet, but she is easy to handle once she is in your arms. We have now learnt that she is trying so hard to be brave and, although she is still quite nervous, we are seeing little bits of her cheeky Daxi personality coming through every day.

Sixpence seems to have had very little positive touch or affection before coming to us. She has recently moved in to foster and is happy to take treats from her foster parents but is not quite sure about being stroked yet. She will allow them to put her harness on as long as she is in a quiet corner and things are taken slowly. You can tell she isn't entirely comfortable, but she trusts us enough to allow it and is always very happy to enjoy a little cheese reward afterwards! With continued positive reinforcement, we are confident that this will improve as Sixpence learns that good things can come from new experiences.

Sixpencerelies heavily on other dogs and really enjoys being around her resident dog friends. She watches what they do and follows their lead for confidence, and she has even learnt from them how to use the dog steps to get onto the sofa and watch the world go by from the front window! She will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home that she can lean on as she continues to find her confidence and learn about home life.

Penny is also discovering all sorts of things that she enjoys. She loves sunbathing, having the freedom to explore a secure dog field, stuffed teddies and, of course, cheese! She has a crate set up with a fluffy bed where she can go when she wants some quiet time to herself, and she seems to really enjoy having this safe space available to her.

Sixpence will need a calm and quiet home with adopters who have breed experience and understand that she will need plenty of time, patience and encouragement as she settles in. Her ideal home would have one or more small, friendly dog companions who can help her feel secure. We feel that children would be too overwhelming for Penny, so she will need an adult-only home.

Penny has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be kind and patient as she continues to learn about home life, including house training. She will also need to continue her harness and lead training at her own pace, as these are still very new experiences for her.

Sixpence is a very sweet little girl who is trying her very best to be brave. She has already made some lovely progress in the short time she has been with us, and we can't wait to see just how much more of her personality comes out as her confidence grows. She just needs someone willing to give her the time, space and love she needs to discover how wonderful her new life can be.

Sixpence has been given the Gift of Life by Sarah Maddox, on behalf of Jesus Christ

We have had Sixpence or 'Penny' as she is known here for a little over a week. it is clear that she has had very little positive touch or affection before and she is trying desperately to be brave!

Although she is still quite nervous were are noticing her trying or learning something new everyday and her cheeky little Daxi personality is starting to shine. She has discovered a love for sunbathing, the freedom of a secure dog field, stuffed teddies and cheese!

Penny is happy to take treats from us but isn't currently sure on being stroked. We can put a harness on her as long as we find a quiet corner and go slow. you can tell she isn't entirely comfortable but let's us do it and enjoys her cheese reward afterwards. We have every confidence that this will improve with more positive reinforcement and learning just how amazing walks are.

She really enjoys being around her resident dog friends and follows what they do for confidence. She's even learnt from them how to get up onto the sofas with the dog steps and watch the world go by out of the front window. We have a crate set up in our dining room with a fluffy bed in for when she wants some time to herself which she likes.

Penny's ideal home would be a quiet one with one or more small dog friends and owners that are willing to give this girl the time and space she needs to learn her new life at her own pace. Sadly we think she would find children too overwhelming. We can't wait to see her confidence grow in her new life.

Sixpence is a nervous girl who has come to us from a breeder. She isn’t brave enough to approach you just yet, but she is easy to handle once she is in your arms. She will need time, patience and plenty of trust-building before she feels confident enough to come out of her shell.

Sixpence relies heavily on other dogs and will follow their lead, so she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home that she can lean on as she learns about home life and finds her paws. She will need a calm and quiet home, with adopters who have breed experience and can understand her needs.

Sixpence has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be kind and patient as she learns about house training. She is working with her kennel mummy on harness training and would like to continue this in her new home. She can live with sensible, dog-savvy teens aged 13+ who will give her the time and space she needs. Sixpence is a very sweet girl who just needs someone willing to give her the chance to blossom.

name: Sunny
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog my size or larger to help me settle in & I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have an undershot jaw & I have had 4 of my teeth removed during spay!

27-08-26 Sunny is a sweet girl who has come to us from a breeder and is trying her hardest to be brave. She was very briefly adopted, but after a few days in her new home it was clear that her and the resident dog weren't a good match and so she has returned to our care.

Sunny loves other dogs and still looks to her kennel friends for comfort and reassurance, so she will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to and lean on as she continues to grow in confidence. She will be best suited to a home where any resident dogs were her size or larger and were fairly confident and well socialised. We think she will settle quickly in the right home, and with patience and encouragement, we’re sure her lovely personality will really begin to shine.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace.She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who are kind and sensible and will give her the time she needs to settle in.She will now happily approach you for a fuss and is easy to handle, which is lovely to see as she begins to settle in and discover the world around her. Sunny arrived with us very matted, but she was such a good girl during her grooming session and took everything in her stride.

Sunny has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be kind and patient as she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She has started to learn all about walking on a lead and harness and though this is still new to her, she is doing well. Sunny is an amazing lady who has so much to look forward to and will make a wonderful addition to a loving and accepting home.

Sunny has arrived with an undershot jaw that does not seem to bother her, but will need to be monitored in her new home. She has had 4 teeth removed at the time of her spay.

Sunny has been given the Gift of Life by Victoria Charlton

Sunny has been on my section for more or less the whole time she’s been at the rescue, and I know we’re not supposed to have favourites, but I just love her so much! She’s SO comical and has such an infectious energy. She can make me laugh and smile by doing absolutely nothing. I can’t explain it, she’s just funny!

She absolutely loves toys and lights up every morning when I bring them to her kennel. She checks on every one and then will pick her favourite one and carry it into bed with her. So sweet! She also loves being in bed. Especially when she’s snuggled up with one of her kennel friends. Her favourite thing in the whole world though, is definitely food. She is such a greedy little monster when it comes to treat time or breakfast or dinner time. She will do pretty much anything if she knows she’ll get a yummy snack out of it. I’ve recently started harness training with her and this has been a huge help. I always have liver paste on hand and she’s doing so well with it. We’re still only walking around quiet places of the rescue currently, so she’s definitely not a pro yet, but she’s getting there!

If you have a house full of toys, love and cosy beds, please consider welcoming this cheeky little darling.

Sunny is a sweet girl who has come to us from a breeder and is trying her hardest to be brave. She was very briefly adopted, but after a few days in her new home it was clear that her and the resident dog weren't a good match and so she has returned to our care.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who are kind and sensible and will give her the time she needs to settle in. She will now happily approach you for a fuss and is easy to handle, which is lovely to see as she begins to settle in and discover the world around her. Sunny arrived with us very matted, but she was such a good girl during her grooming session and took everything in her stride.

name: Candy
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I can live with larger, playful resident dogs, or I can be the only dog in the home!

I would like a large, and secure garden with 6ft+ fences.

I walk well on a lead, but I can be strong so my adopters will need to work with this

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home! Read below for more!

Candy is a very sweet and affectionate lady who has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for her forever home. She absolutely adores attention and cuddles and, once she gets to know you, it doesn't take her long to show just how loving she really is. Candy simply wants to be close to her people and has completely stolen the hearts of everyone she has met. She has blossomed into the most loving girl and will make a wonderful companion and is sure to become the ultimate cuddle bug in the home.

Candy has built a lovely bond with the staff member who has worked closely with her since she first arrived. She truly trusts her and has come on so much since arriving with us. Candy has such a sweet nature and it is clear how much she enjoys spending time with people she knows and trusts.

Her lead walking has improved so much too. She is now walking much better and really enjoys her outings, although her adopters will need to continue working on her lead manners so she can enjoy plenty of adventures. She has even started joining a regular volunteer on walks. Although, she doesn't completely trust him just yet, she is beginning to learn to trust him and build a relationship.

Candy mixes well with polite, well mannered dogs however she can sometimes be a little selective with choosing her friends. She doesn’t appreciate when dogs are over the top but when she does make a new friend her own play style can be quite full on! She comes away when called so we are always able to calm her down for a tasty treat. Because of her size and excitable nature, she would not be able to live with smaller breeds of dogs in the home and will need a home without cats.

As Candy is a very large lady, it is important that her adopters have experience with a similar breed and understand her needs. We have found that she can be particularly worried by formal handling, such as veterinary examinations, and finds these situations quite stressful. We will be muzzle training Candy so that she can be safely and comfortably handled for occasions such as vet visits. She recently needed to visit the vet due to sore ears and, although she found having her ears examined uncomfortable, she coped very well with the support of people she knows and trusts. She did also need to visit the vet for a check up on a day when her regular person wasn't around and found it much harder to cope with and became extremely stressed and agitated. She takes so much comfort from her known and trusted people.

Candy would be best suited to an adult-only home where her adopters can give her the time and space she needs to build trust and settle in.

Candy has arrived with a scab on the right side of her face that will be addressed during the time of her spay and is being treated for a ear infection.

Candy has come such a long way since arriving with us and is now so ready for a loving home of her own. She is an absolute angel and a true credit to her breed, with so much love and affection to give. She truly deserves someone who will give her the love, patience and happiness she deserves.

Candy will need more than one meet and greet with her prospective adopters to allow her time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Candy has been given the Gift of Life by Carolina Olsen

The bond I’ve built with this lovely, sweet girl is unmatched. I feel so honoured by how much trust she has given me. She really is like my best friend, and I just love spending my days with her.

Candy is such a sweet girl, but she can be wary of strangers and a little head shy, especially when new people reach over her head to give her a fuss. Whenever we're out walking and people ask to say hello, I always explain that she's head shy and ask them to let her sniff them first and approach her at her own pace. She is more than happy to take treats from people, and it's lovely to see her little interactions.

To help build her confidence with new people, Candy now goes out with one of our regular volunteers twice a week for longer walks. She doesn't trust him 100% just yet, but she'll happily go out walking with him and take treats. She's still very aware of his presence, but it's all about time, patience and allowing her to build that trust in her own time.

Candy also had her first bath with us this week! Although she wasn't too keen to begin with, she trusted me and I made sure to respect her boundaries. We managed to wash her from the shoulders down, and I'm super proud of her! The hairdryer was a definite no, but that's absolutely fine. We do everything at Candy's pace.

She's also learnt to sit, and one of her favourite things to do is play with the squeaky balls in the yard.

Candy really does feel like my best friend at the rescue. She always makes me smile, keeps me pushing through and has such a special place in my heart. I feel so lucky to have built the bond we have, and I can't wait to see her continue to grow in confidence.

Candy is an absolute angel and a true credit to her breed. I’ve worked with her since she first arrived at the rescue, and over that time we’ve built such a lovely bond. She truly trusts me and knows that I only have her best interests at heart.

Candy has blossomed into the most loving and affectionate girl, and I genuinely love spending my days with her. She has such a sweet nature and has come on so much since arriving with us.

Candy recently had a vet visit due to having sore ears. Although you could tell she was uncomfortable while the vet was examining them, she was such a good girl throughout, and I was incredibly proud of her.

She has also mixed with quite a few dogs here at the rescue and has been brilliant with all of them. She can sometimes be a little bouncy and excitable when first meeting new dogs, but she listens when asked to calm down and is learning to manage her excitement really well.

Her lead walking has improved so much too, and she’s now walking much better and enjoying her outings.

Candy has come such a long way and is so ready for a loving home of her own. She truly deserves someone who will give her the love, patience and happiness she deserves.

Candy is a very sweet and affectionate lady who has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for her forever home. She absolutely adores attention and cuddles and, once she gets to know you, it doesn't take her long to show just how loving she really is. Candy simply wants to be close to her people and has completely stolen the hearts of everyone she has met. She will make a wonderful companion and is sure to become the ultimate cuddle bug in the home.

Candy can walk on a lead, although she can be quite strong, so her adopters will need to be prepared to continue her training and help her develop her lead manners so she can enjoy plenty of adventures. As she is a very large lady, it is important that her adopters have experience with her breed and understand her needs.

Candy has the confidence to be the only dog in the home, although she could potentially live with another large breed dog following a successful meet and greet. She loves to play and can be quite excitable, so she would not be suitable to live with smaller or more fragile dogs and she will need a home without cats.

Candy is an incredible girl, but she can be sensitive when she is worried or when she feels uncomfortable, for this reason, we feel she would be best suited to an adult-only home where her adopters can give her the time and space she needs to build trust and settle in.

She has arrived with a scab on the right side of her face that will be addressed during the time of her spay.

name: Crispin
description:
I would like a calm and quiet home where I can settle in.

I would prefer to be the only dog in the home. I don't mind cats!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and love being out and about!

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

Crispin originally came to us from a breeder last October. He was adopted for a few months but returned to our care after his adopters sadly realised they were not the right match for him. Although they gave him every opportunity to settle, Crispin remained very worried whenever the male in the household was home and struggled to relax in his company.

Since returning to us, Crispin has moved into foster and has settled beautifully. He is an incredibly loving, cuddly little boy who simply wants to be close to his people. While he can initially be worried by some men, his foster carer has found that once visitors give him some attention, he quickly relaxes and happily cuddles up with them. He does the same with female visitors. He has adult grandsons in his foster home and, after an initial bark, is very happy to settle down with them.

Crispin does get on with other dogs, but he can be quite keen to push his way in for attention and may grumble if another dog gets in the way. He is not aggressive and, having no teeth, cannot bite, but he would be best suited to being homed as an only dog. His foster carer feels he would particularly enjoy being the centre of his person's world, as he simply loves being with his human, male or female.

Crispin absolutely loves his walks and this is his favourite pastime. He gets wonderfully excited when it is time to go out and walks beautifully on both a lead and harness. He is sociable with other dogs he meets, enjoys exploring new places and travels well in the car. He particularly loves visiting the coffee shop and is happiest when he can be out and about with his people.

As Crispin has now experienced life in a home, he has settled well into a routine and sleeps soundly through the night. He has had the occasional wee indoors first thing in the morning, although this has been improving, so his adopters should continue his house training with patience and consistency.

Crispin forms incredibly strong bonds with his favourite people and loves to be close by and involved in everything they are doing. He showed signs of separation anxiety in his previous home when left for more than a couple of hours, so his ideal home would be one where someone is around for most of the day and any time alone can be built up gradually.

Crispin has a cataract in his right eye and is developing one in his left. Despite this, he gets around brilliantly and you would hardly know he has eyesight problems. He has also had all of his teeth removed and will need to remain on a soft diet for life. He has Grade 2 patella luxation in both hind legs, which may continue to improve with gentle exercise as

Crispin has a travel document, which says he is 7 years old, but we do feel he could potentially be a little older than this.

Crispin has been given the Gift of Life by Katrina Pirner

Crispin is looking for his own special human where he can be the ONLY dog and have all the love and affection for himself. Although he is in foster with other dogs, we think he would now prefer to be the only dog in the home.

Crispin has recently spent a few days with another fosterer as I was on holiday and attached himself to the lady of the house and wasn't interested in the other 5 dogs or man of the house just the lady.

He walks perfectly on the lead and loves to go out as many times as you're willing to take him, equally though he loves to potter in the garden alongside his fosterer whilst she's raking up leaves. He loves to settle inside either on your lap or close by on the sofa.

Crispin enjoys all foods though some treats have to be in small pieces as he has no teeth but he eats either wet food or kibble with warm water to mash it down. His cataract doesn't affect him at all. Although Crispin is 7 he has the energy and zest for life of a much younger dog. He can literally walk for hours.

Crispin would love a one person, male or female, calm household where he can soak up all the attention from his special human. Although he gets on with all dogs outside of the home, he prefers to be cuddled up with his human wherever it may be.. sofa, bed he s not fussed as long as he knows they are close by him.

Crispin walks perfectly on a harness and lead and is good off lead too. He will walk ahead of you but keep coming back to 'check in' with you.

Crispin continues to thrive in his foster home and is loving this home life. He loves his food, loves his walks, loves his cuddles and just loves everything to be honest.

Although Crispin lives alongside his foster sisters, I do feel he would love a home with no other dogs and just a single active  adult home, male or female, where he can have all the attention and love. Cats are fine, as he dosen't take any notice of them.

Although his initial write states that he may be older than 7 I feel he is aged about right apart from his lack of teeth as he is full of energy and  fun.

Crispin is smashing this home life. He is an absolute gentleman and will make a perfect best friend for an active person who is at home most of the time.

This week he has visited various secure fields, visited coffee shops and even popped into a pub for a cool drink while out on a street walk. He loves to be out and about with his human and then return home for snuggles on the sofa.

Although Crispin has a cataract in his right eye this does not seem to affect him at all. His luxating patellas also don't seem to bother him and his movement is 100%.

Crispin recently moved foster homes through no fault of his own. He is a gorgeous, well mannered, cuddly boy who loves his walks, his humans and his food.

He gets along with the cats and dogs in my home, though initially Crispin demanded all the attention and would push the other dogs out of the way to get his cuddles first but with careful handling this has improved over the week.

He loves to cuddle up on my bed with my own dogs and sleeps all night there. He lives for his walks and gets very excited when his lead/harness appear. He can walk on his own or with another dog for company.

He happily shares his food bowl with his foster friend Lemon Pie. Even the cats dig in with him sometimes. He is getting used to being left when I go shopping and I am extending these trips so he gets used to being without humans for a while. Crispin does bark initially when visitors come into my home but this soon subsides when he realises they will do him no harm. Keep up the good work Crispin, you've got this my boy

Crispin has been back in foster care for a week and has settled in beautifully. He is an incredibly loving, cuddly little boy who simply wants to be loved. Sadly, he was returned because he became anxious and barked whenever the man in the household moved around.

He walks beautifully on a lead and harness, sleeps soundly through the night alongside the other foster dog, and travels well. Although he is perfectly happy living with other dogs, he could also be an only dog so he can enjoy all the cuddles and affection he deserves. He has had a few little accidents indoors first thing in the morning, but over the last few days he has settled into a much better routine.

Crispin has no teeth, so he will need to remain on a soft diet for the rest of his life. He also has a cataract in one eye and the beginnings of a cataract in the other, but you would hardly know he has any sight issues as he gets around so well.

He really is a very special little boy who simply needs a loving home where he can feel safe, secure, and cherished.

Crispin originally came to us from a breeder last October. He was adopted for a few months but has come back into our care after his adopters sadly realised they were not the right match for him. Although they gave him every opportunity to settle, Crispin remained very worried whenever the male in the household was home and simply couldn't relax in his company.Crispin is a dear little boy who can still be worried and unsure at times. It is clear that he had very little socialisation in the past, and although he has made lovely progress since living in a home, he still needs patient adopters who understand that building trust takes time. He can be touch-sensitive when he is feeling anxious, so gentle handling and allowing him to approach in his own time will help him continue to gain confidence.Crispin will be best suited to adopters who understand the needs of scared ex-breeding dogs and who will give him all the time he needs to settle at his own pace. He would be happy to share his home with another kind and confident resident dog in his new home. However, in the right home, with owners who are around enough to reassure him and who have experience with ex-breeding dogs, he could also be the only dog in the home.One thing Crispin has discovered is just how much he loves going for walks! He gets wonderfully excited when it's time to head out, twirling around and eagerly waiting by the front door. Once out, he walks beautifully on a lead, is very sociable with other dogs he meets, enjoys exploring new places, and travels well in the car. Walking has become one of his favourite activities and is a lovely way to watch his confidence shine through.As Crispin has now experienced life in a home, he has become familiar with many of the sights and sounds of everyday living. However, he hasn't quite mastered house training yet, so his adopters will need to continue helping him learn with patience, consistency, and plenty of encouragement.Crispin has also shown that he forms incredibly strong bonds with his favourite person. He loves to be close by and wants to be involved in everything they are doing. Because of this, he showed signs of separation anxiety in his previous home when left for more than a couple of hours. His ideal home would therefore be one where someone is around for most of the day, and where any time left alone can be built up very gradually, helping him feel safe and secure.Crispin has a cataract in his right eye and is developing a cataract in his left eye. He has had dental work and unfortunately did need to have all of his teeth removed, so he will need to stay on a soft diet for the rest of his life. He has Grade 2 patella luxation in both hind legs, although this may continue to improve with gentle exercise as he builds muscle.Crispin is a gentle soul who has had a difficult start in life, but he has already shown that, with kindness and patience, he is capable of making wonderful progress. He is looking for a very special person who will understand his worries, celebrate his achievements, and enjoy watching him continue to blossom into the loyal and loving companion we know he can be.Crispin has a travel document, which says he is 7 years old, but we do feel he could be a little older than this.

name: Lucy
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I don't mind cats!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Lucy is a very worried lady who has come to us from a breeder and is still learning that people can be kind and caring. She desperately wants to be brave but finds the world a very scary place, and can be vocal when people she doesn't know approach her. Once she gets to know you and feels comfortable with you being around, she does settle and can be calm and quiet in your presence. Lucy is such a precious girl who just needs time, patience and understanding to help her find her confidence.

Lucy is very active and playful with her kennel friends, and although she doesn't yet ask for a fuss, she will come over for a little sniff when her friends approach you. She is a girl who will need to take things at her own pace, and she has started harness training but is still learning what is expected of her. Lucy would love a home that can offer her an active lifestyle once she has had time to settle, along with at least one kind and confident resident dog who she can look to for reassurance as she learns about home life.

Lucy has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be patient as she learns about house training and walking on a lead. She enjoys her food and is fed separately here, although she is happy to take treats alongside other dogs. Lucy will need a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and where her needs will be understood and she can be given the time, space and security she needs to blossom. We would consider homing her with dog savvy teenagers 16+. She has met cats fine at the rescue, and could live with a dog-savvy cat who doesn't mind sharing their space.

With patience, kindness and the support of a confident canine friend, we hope Lucy will slowly learn to trust and become the most wonderful companion.

Lucy has been given the gift of life by Linda Towers

This absolutely stunning girl is Lucy and she is one girl who is absolutely breaking my heart. She desperately wants to be brave but doesn't understand that humans are actually kind and caring.

She's very unsure about people being around her that she doesn't know and can be vocal because of this, when she knows you and is happy with you existing around her then she does settle and will be calm and quiet in your presence.She needs to learn everything, she's started harness training but doesn't understand it yet and although she doesn't ask for a fuss, she will come over when her kennel friends do and have a bit of a sniff of you. She does like food and is fed separately here, but she's fine having treats with other dogs. She is honestly so precious and in the right home I can see her being the most wonderful companion, she just needs time and patience and to be kept safe in the process of gaining her confidence in this big scary world.

Lucy is a very worried lady who has come to us from a breeder and is understandably nervous around people. She can be quite vocal when approached and doesn’t yet enjoy being handled, she prefers to keep her distance while she works out that people can be trusted. Lucy is a sweet girl underneath her worries and will need plenty of TLC, patience and understanding from her new family as she begins to build her confidence.

Lucy is very active and playful with her kennel friends, and this is where we get to see a little more of her personality. She would love a home that can offer her an active lifestyle once she has had time to settle and feel comfortable. She will also need at least one kind and confident resident dog who she can look to and lean on for reassurance as she learns about home life and gains confidence.

Lucy has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be patient as she learns about house training and walking on a lead. These things may take some time, and she will need a family who is willing to go at her pace without putting pressure on her. Lucy will need an adult-only home with ex-breeding experience, where her needs will be understood and she can have the time and space she needs to blossom. With patience, love and the support of a confident canine friend, we hope Lucy will slowly learn to trust and show us the wonderful girl hiding underneath her worries.

name: Rosco
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I can be an only dog or live with female dogs. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden with 6ft+ fencing.

I can walk well on a lead and would love an active home.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have a lump near my eye which causes some irritation and will be assessed.

17-11-26 Rosco has come to us from a breeder to find his forever home, having originally come from Romania a few years ago. He is a sweet natured boy who, despite all the changes in his world, is settling in well and taking everything in his stride. He loves being around humans and is so much fun to spend time with.

Rosco will be looking for a home with adopters who have experience with dogs of similar breeders and will let him settle in at his own pace. We would consider homing him with gentle dog savvy teenagers aged 13+. He can bark a little when left, so this is something that his adopters will need to work on with him, building up the time he is left alone.

Rosco is quite confident and would be more than happy to be homed as an only dog, where he can get all of the fuss and attention he desires. He also gets along well with other dogs and we would consider homing him with a female resident dog. He can walk on a lead and would enjoy an active home where he can get out and about and explore the world with his new family.

He has never lived in a home before, so his adopters will need to be kind and understanding as he settles into home life and learns new skills such as house training.

With a little time, patience and lots of love, we hope Rosco will soon discover just how wonderful life in a forever home can be.

He has arrived with a wart in the corner of his left eye, which is causing some irritation and will be assessed by our vets.

name: Nicole
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

Nicole has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for her forever home. She was very scared when she first arrived and had clearly had little handling or socialisation, making human contact very worrying for her.

Nicole briefly moved into a foster home to learn about home life but returned to us following one incident where she became tangled in her lead and harness, panicked and nipped her fosterer. This was a single incident during a frightening experience, but adopters must understand that she can panic if she feels trapped or overwhelmed.

Nicole has now been back at the rescue for just over a month and is making lovely progress. She still doesn't like being picked up or handled, but is much better than she was and is increasingly comfortable spending time around people she trusts. She enjoys sitting in the play yard with her trusted people and responds brilliantly to treats, which are helping to build her confidence. She is a curious, cheeky little character who loves food, toys and snoozing in her bed, and she is even trying hard to be kennel clean.

Nicole loves other dogs and takes comfort from their presence, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog to help her feel secure and act as a role model.

She needs a calm, quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of nervous ex-breeding dogs. As she has never successfully experienced home life, she will need patience with house training and learning the basics of being a pet. Lead and harness training will also need to be introduced very carefully because of her previous experience.

Nicole still has a long way to go, but her curiosity and wonderful personality are beginning to shine through. With the right home, canine companion and plenty of time and understanding, we hope she will continue to blossom.

Our vets noted a slightly unusual heart rhythm, and a heart scan showed mild valve changes. She currently requires no treatment and is expected to live a normal, happy life, although routine heart checks and monitoring for future symptoms are recommended. She has been treated for a ear infection.

Nicole has been given the Gift of Life by Shirley Bourne

Nicole has been back at the rescue with me for just over a month now, and even though she is still a scared lady, I can definitely see she has made progress. She still doesn’t like to be picked up and handled, but she’s a lot better with it now than she was when she first arrived. She’s also more content just being in my presence now and will happily hang out with me in the play yard with confidence. I spend a lot of time sitting on the floor with her and dishing out treats every so often to stay in her good books. She does love her food, so this helps massively with building some trust with her!

Nicole does still have a long way to go until she’s anywhere near being a ‘normal’ dog, but she has a lot of curiosity in her and definitely some Shih Tzu attitude as well, so I’m hoping she will blossom in the right home. If you have lots of time and patience, and a space in your heart and home to welcome a special lady, please consider Nicole. I promise you won’t regret it!

Nicole is the type of dog that can instantly put a smile on your face, even when she’s not doing anything. She has such a comical and infectious energy, and I really just love spending time with her. She loves snoozing in bed in her kennel through the day and playing with toys too. She even tries her hardest to be kennel clean!! She’s very easy to look after day to day. So please… give her a chance.

Nicole has been in foster for a week and is a sweetie. She has a wonderfully inquisitive nature and loves investigating everything around her, which makes us chuckle! She is still very nervous about being handled and will bark when she's feeling unsure, but she is already making progress. She now takes treats from us and absolutely loves her food. She is also mostly clean overnight.

Nicole has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for her forever home. She is a lovely little girl who is understandably feeling very scared and overwhelmed to find herself here. It’s clear she hasn’t had much handling or socialisation before, so human hands are quite worrying for her at the moment, but we will continue gently helping her learn that hands can be kind.

Nicole will be looking for a calm and quiet adult only home where she can settle in at her own pace. She would really benefit from adopters who have experience with nervous ex-breeding dogs and who understand the patience, time and reassurance she will need as she learns to trust.

She loves other dogs and takes great comfort from their presence, so Nicole will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help her feel safe and secure.

As Nicole has never lived in a home before, she will need patient adopters who are ready to help her learn everything about home life from the very beginning. She will need to learn new skills like house training and will also need to learn all about walking on a lead and harness.

With time, kindness and plenty of TLC, Nicole will begin to grow in confidence and let her personality shine.

Our vets have noted that Nicole has a slightly unusual heart rhythm, so she underwent a heart scan at our vets which showed some mild valve changes. At this stage she does not require any treatment and is expected to live a normal, happy life, although we would recommend routine heart checks and monitoring for any future symptoms.

name: Tippins
description:
I would like a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need another dog my size or larger in my new home.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk on lead but I can be spooked. Let's take it slow!

I have spent some time in a home, but still have lots to learn.

Tippins is a lovely lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She can be apprehensive when meeting new people and may bark at strangers, but once she feels comfortable, her wonderful personality shines through. She has formed lovely bonds with staff at the rescue and, once attached to someone, she adores cuddles and wants to be as close to her favourite people as possible. She is a ridiculously affectionate girl who gives her whole heart to those she trusts.

Tippins was briefly adopted as an only dog, but has sadly returned to our care as she really struggled without another dog by her side. Although she didn't appear to rely on other dogs for comfort in kennels, she became very shut down in the home and struggled to come out of her shell. We therefore feel she will need a calm and confident resident dog, her size or larger, to act as a role model and help her settle. She isn't particularly cuddly with other dogs, but she shares her kennel well and we believe having another dog around will help her feel more secure while she adjusts to her new surroundings.

Tippins walks beautifully on her harness alongside her handler, although busy places and traffic can still make her nervous. Her new family should continue her confidence-building with quiet walks and plenty of reassurance.

Although she has spent some time in a home, Tippins had never experienced home life before her adoption and so her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she learns all about home life and house training. She will need a quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and understand that settling into a home may take her some time. Once she feels secure, she will try her very best to be brave and become a devoted companion.

Tippins can live with teenagers aged 16 and over who are sensible and able to respect her need for a gentle introduction. Her adopters should also be prepared to welcome her onto the furniture, as we suspect this affectionate girl will thoroughly enjoy being close to her people once she feels safe.

Tippins has returned to us with an ear infection and is currently receiving treatment. Our vets are monitoring her ears and will continue to provide any treatment she needs. She will need her ears to be monitored and cared for in her new home as appropriate.

Tippins is a very special little lady who has made fantastic progress with us. With the right canine role model, an experienced and peaceful home, and the time she needs to settle, we hope she will finally discover just how wonderful life can be.

Tippins has been with me for more or less the whole time she’s been at the rescue and I honestly couldn’t love her anymore if I tried. Getting to spend time with her every day is an absolute privilege and I’m so grateful I get to look after her until she finds her forever home. She makes me laugh and smile every day and our cuddle sessions are my favourite thing in the whole world. I don’t think I’ve ever known a rescue dog to be as affectionate with me as she is. She literally just wants to be as close to me as possible at all times, and she also gives the best kisses!

Tippins can still be a little standoffish when she first meets new people, but at the rescue it doesn’t take her long to drop her guard with them. She did however struggle when she was briefly adopted. She was in the home for 3 weeks and sadly she just completely shut down. She hid in her safe place for the whole time and couldn’t find it in her to approach her new mum. She was adopted as an only dog, so we’re not sure if not being around another dog was the issue.

She’s not reliant on dogs at the rescue and she’s definitely more human focused, but because we don’t want a repeat of what happened last time, we are looking to home her with a resident dog. She can get a little jealous over attention, so a dog her size or larger would be the best fit. She’s never done anything and I do think she’ll be absolutely fine once she settles in and finds her feet, but it’s just something her future adopters should keep in mind!

Tippins walks perfectly to heal on a lead and also really, really enjoys her time in our secure yards. She loves to run around after me and frolic around without a care in the world. It’s lovely to see and it really gives me a glimpse of what her life could be like in her forever home. I hope she doesn’t have to wait much longer.

I’ve worked with a LOT of dogs over my 7 years of being at the rescue, and when I say this girl is really something special, I truly mean it. She’s a ray of sunshine on a cloudy day, a shoulder to cry on when you need it, and a breath of fresh air always. I adore everything about her and I will genuinely be very jealous of her future family.

She deserves to be absolutely cherished and doted on for the rest of her life, and loved unconditionally. Please don’t keep her waiting too long.

Tippins has been with me for about a month now, and I have really, REALLY fallen for her. Even though she presents as a nervous girl and will bark at strangers, it doesn’t take her long to let her guard down at all. When she does, she is your best friend, your shadow, your snuggle buddy... and you are her whole world. She absolutely adores the people she loves and really gives her whole heart to us. She is ridiculously affectionate, and I fear she’s so wasted being in kennels.

Tippins walks beautifully on a harness right by my side and looks up at me to check in constantly. She can still be nervous in busy places and around traffic, but that is something that she’ll get used to in time. I would recommend her adopters do some practice in the garden first before they venture out, and definitely establish a bond with her first.

Even though Tippins has never been in a home before, I’m pretty certain she’s going to want to join everyone on the furniture for snuggles, so this must be welcomed with open arms. Every day with me, she jumps up onto the bench next to me in the play yard, and she loves it when I sit in her bed in her kennel with her. So she’s a cuddler for sure!!

Please don’t keep this very special girl waiting for too much longer. She deserves to be loved and in a home so much.

Tippins is a lovely lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is a little apprehensive when she first meets new people, but she is already showing signs that her confidence is growing. Once she knows you, she enjoys a fuss and is happy to be handled. Tippins has a big personality and is a fun girl to spend time with.At the moment, Tippins is feeling a little less brave and is finding comfort in the company of her kennel friends. We feel it would be best for her to be rehomed with at least one other confident resident dog for support and companionship. She has always lived with bigger dogs and seems happiest around them. Tippins can be a little bossy with less confident dogs, so she wouldn't be suitable to live with smaller or younger dogs. We will continue to assess her confidence while she is with us to see if she could adapt to being an only dog. She will need adopters with ex-breeding experience that can understand her needs.As Tippins has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient while she settles in and learns what home life is all about. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens, aged 16+ that can allow her time to settle into a calm environment.Tippins already walks on a lead, but doesn't seem to be overly confident on this so she will need continued support as she learns, and once she has settled into her new home, she would enjoy one or two walks around the local area with her resident dog so that she can continue lead training.Tippins is a lovely girl with lots of character. She's already showing us what a sweet dog she is, and we hope that, with time and patience, she'll continue to grow in confidence and enjoy everything home life has to offer.Tippins is now receiving regular cleanings from the vets for waxy ears and this will need to be monitored in her new home.

name: Yasmin
description:
I can live with older, dog savvy teenagers, aged 16+ who respect my space.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have had 6 teeth extracted and an umbilical hernia repair.

22-10-26 Yasmin is a quiet little girl who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She seems a little overwhelmed by her new surroundings, but she has been accepting of handling and is not overly scared. Yasmin is a shy girl who will need time, patience and gentle encouragement to help her feel safe and begin to build her confidence. However, the longer she has been with us, she has built some confidence and will approach to take some treat paste from you.

Yasmin would do well with a kind and gentle resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws. Having a friendly canine companion by her side should help her feel more secure as she adjusts to life in a home. Her adopters will need to have experience with ex-breeders to better understand her needs. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16 and over who are sensible.

As Yasmin has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be understanding and allow her to progress at her own pace.

Yasmin has had 6 teeth extracted at the time of her spay as well as an umbilical hernia repair.

With a calm, loving home and a little patience, we hope Yasmin will gradually grow in confidence and discover the comforts of being a cherished family member.

name: Fallon
description:
I will need an adult-only home that understands me.

I would prefer to be the only dog in the home!

I will need a secure garden, with at least 6ft+ fencing to explore!

I am new to lead walking, and would like to continue this once I have settled in.

I have lived in a home before, but may need some reminders.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

05-11-26 Fallon is a super sweet and clever girl who originally came to us from a breeder but was sadly returned after struggling to cope with visitors coming and going in her previous home. She is a sensitive lady who can find changes to her environment and unexpected interactions difficult, but she has made wonderful progress with us and has formed some lovely bonds with her main carers. Once she knows and trusts you, her silly, playful personality really starts to shine, and she gives the very best snuggles!

Fallon can mix with other dogs but would prefer to have her own space in a home, so she is looking to be the only dog. She walks well on a lead, although she can occasionally walk in circles when feeling anxious or excited. She may also bark back if another dog reacts towards her. Fallon can be sensitive when resting and has previously startled and made contact when someone sat beside her on the sofa, so her adopters will need to understand her boundaries and give her quiet, undisturbed places to relax.

Fallon is looking for an adult-only home with at least 6ft secure fencing, where her adopters have previous ex-breeding experience and a good understanding of Collies and their sensitive nature. She will need a calm environment, predictable routines and cosy bed spaces where she can retreat when she needs some quiet time.

Fallon really is a lovely girl with so much personality, and it is wonderful to see how far she has come. She just needs someone who understands her needs, respects her space and is willing to give her the time to settle. In return, they will discover a clever, playful and incredibly affectionate companion who has so much love to give!

Fallon has been given the Gift of Life by Carolina Olsen

name: Sianon
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Sianon has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for her forever home. She is a worried girl who is unsure around humans and isn't used to being handled yet. She is going to need plenty of love, patience and TLC as she settles in and slowly begins to grow in confidence.

She has recently moved to a wonderful foster home where she is getting to experience home life for the first time and is settling in well. She is a very sweet girl who is trying so hard to be brave but is not yet comfortable being handled. She is happy to explore the home and garden but will head in the opposite direction if she sees anyone approaching. She loves her food and treats and is very interested when they appear.

Sianon will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who understand that she will need time to adjust to her new life. Her new family will need to be kind and patient, allowing her to settle in at her own pace without putting pressure on her.

Sianon relies on other dogs for confidence, so she will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend and help her feel safe. She loves to snuggle with the other dogs in her foster home,

She has never lived in a home before moving to foster, so everything will be new to her, and she will need gentle guidance as she learns all about home life and new skills such as house training. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness and will need to practice first around the home and garden until she is feeling brave enough to venture further.

Sianon is a gentle girl who has lots to learn, but with the right home, a patient family and a lovely canine friend to show her the ropes, we hope she will gradually discover her confidence and enjoy all the wonderful things life has to offer.

Sianon has been given the Gift of Life by Dee Wickson-Dix

Sianon is settling into foster. She is a sweet little girl who tries her best to be brave but is not yet comfortable at being handled. She's happy to explore the home and garden but will head in the opposite direction if she sees anyone approaching. She mixes well with all my dogs and loves to snuggle up with them. She is interested in food and will follow when she sees her dinner arriving but will wait until I leave before approaching it. She knows when the treat tin comes out and whilst she won't take a treat from me will wait for me to drop it and then quickly retrieve it.

Sianon will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who understand that she will need time to adjust. Her new family will need to be kind and patient, allowing her to settle in at her own pace without putting pressure on her. She has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her, and she will need gentle guidance as she learns all about home life and new skills such as house training and how to walk on a lead and harness.

Sianon relies on other dogs for confidence, so she will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend and help her feel safe. We hope having a canine companion by her side will help her learn that the world isn't such a scary place. Any children in the home will need to be teenagers aged 16+.

name: Koala
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I am spayed and have had 4 teeth extracted,

Koala is a worried little girl who has come to us from a breeder. When she first arrived she was very frightened and unsure of humans, but since then she has started to settle in and has started to come out of her shell. She was quite flighty and would choose to run away and hide if someone approached her.

Koala has recently moved to a wonderful foster home where she is getting to experience home life for the first time ever and is settling in well. She has a very happy, waggy tail and will even follow her fosterer around the home. She will approach her when she is sitting down, but isn't quite brave enough to accept a stroke just yet. She has settled very quickly into a routine and especially loves her food.

Koala would benefit from a calm and quiet home with adopters with experience of scared ex-breeding dogs. She could be homed witholder, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who are sensible and understand that she will need plenty of space and patience.

Koala relies on other dogs for comfort and reassurance and so she will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend and help her to settle in and learn to trust.

Koala has never lived in a home before moving to foster, so her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she continues to learn all about home life. She has been clean in the house so far in foster. She hasn't yet started to learn about walking on a lead and harness and will need to practice once she is feeling a little braver.

Koala is a worried girl, but underneath her worries is a little lady who deserves the chance to learn how wonderful life can be. She is looking for someone special who is willing to take a chance on her and give her the time she needs to blossom.

Koala has had 4 teeth extracted at the time of her spay.

Koala has been given the Gift of Life by Margaret Hunter

Koala is a happy, waggy tailed girl. She will follow me around and approach when I'm sitting but isn't yet brave enough to accept a stroke. She is comfortable coming in and out of the house and happy to explore the various rooms. She has quickly settled into a routine and knows which is her spot for dinner. She loves her food, but is happy to share. Koala mixes well with dogs of all sizes. She has been clean in the house. Koala is looking for a home with friendly companions and with adopters who can continue to show her that hands can be kind.

Koala is a frightened little lady who has come to us from a breeder and is still very unsure of us humans. She can be quite a flighty girl and, at the moment, would much rather hide away than have people approach her. Once she is safely in your arms, she is easier to handle, but she will need plenty of time and patience to learn that people can be trusted.

Koala relies heavily on her kennel friends for confidence and comfort, so she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing and help her feel more secure. Having a canine friend by her side will be very important as she begins to experience life outside of kennels.

Koala has never lived in a home before, so she will need understanding adopters who can give her the time she needs to settle in and learn about house training. Lead walking may be far too scary for her initially, so she will need a secure garden where she can safely explore, sniff and build her confidence at her own pace.

Koala can live with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who are sensible and understand that she will need plenty of space and patience. Her adopters will need previous ex-breeding experience so they can better understand her needs and help her adjust to life in a home.

Koala is a very frightened girl, but underneath her worries is a little lady who deserves the chance to learn how wonderful life can be. She is looking for someone special who is willing to take a chance on her and give her the time she needs to blossom.

name: Fanta
description:
I can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who understand I need space.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need a secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before

I've started my vaccinations and will be spayed before adoption.

22-10-26 Fanta is quite a scared girly who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is in need of lots of TLC and the reassurance of a confident resident dog to help her feel safe. Fanta can be a little panicky and flighty, so she will need a very secure garden with high fencing to keep her safe while she settles into her new surroundings.

Although Fanta was shaking, she allowed us to pick her up and give her a gentle fuss to reassure her that we are here to help. She is still very unsure at the moment, so her new family will need to be patient and allow her the time she needs to learn to trust.

Fanta will need another kind and confident dog in her new home, as this will be a much-needed support system for her. A reassuring canine companion can help guide her and give her the confidence she needs as she settles in and begins to find her paws.

As Fanta has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. Her adopters will need to understand that this may take time and be prepared to let her progress at her own pace. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who understand she needs time to settle in. Her adopters will need to have ex-breeding experience to better understand her needs.

Fanta is a very worried little girl, but she has already shown us that she can accept gentle affection even when she is feeling frightened. We hope that with a confident canine companion, a calm environment and lots of patience, she will gradually begin to feel safe and discover the happy new life she deserves.

Fanta has been given the Gift of Life by Aimee Helme
