name: Max
description:
I need an active, breed experienced home that loves playtime!

I’m active and would love a large, secure garden to let off steam.

I walk on the lead but I can pull when excited.

I am house trained but I need to learn some manners.

I have been neutered and am ready for my forever home!

Max is a superstar Lurcher who has been returned to us from his adoptive family. They made the heartbreaking decision to bring him back as he was becoming dominant over the other dog in the home.

He is a very excitable, happy boy - essentially an overgrown puppy in a big body. Max is full of fun and enthusiasm and will need an active home that can meet his exercise and stimulation needs. He already knows some basic commands such as “sit”, “paw”, “lay down”, and “wait”, and he is eager to interact with his people. He is very food oriented, which makes training enjoyable and rewarding, and he already shows lovely food manners, waiting patiently when asked.

Max absolutely loves other dogs and gets incredibly excited when he sees a potential new friend. However, he is still young, full of energy, and not always aware of his size and strength. This can sometimes lead to him becoming overexcited, a little mouthy, and unintentionally overwhelming other dogs. He has been working hard on his social skills and has been socialising while wearing a muzzle for safe and positive interactions. This is purely as a precaution, and his future adopters will need to continue this training and take a responsible approach when introducing him to other dogs.

As he was too much for a more timid dog in his previous home, we feel that Max would be best suited to being homed as an only dog, provided he has plenty of appropriate socialisation with dogs of a similar size and play style. He cannot live with cats or small furries.

As Max has previously lived in a home, he is familiar with household sights and sounds and is house trained. However, he is still working on his lead manners and can pull when he gets excited. Ongoing training, structure, and consistency will be important, along with plenty of mental stimulation to keep his busy mind engaged. He would thrive in a home that can offer activities such as training games or even dog sports.

Max could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over, who understand that he can be a bit of a bull in a china shop. Any young people in the home will need to be confident and not worried by an enthusiastic dog who may jump up while he continues to work on his manners.

Max does struggle with separation anxiety and can become destructive if left alone for long periods, so he will need a home where someone is around most of the time and who is committed to helping him gradually build confidence with being left.

Max's new home will need a large, secure garden with 6ft boundaries, where he can let off some steam.

Max will make an amazing addition to a home with experience of similar breeds. He truly is a lovely boy, bouncy, affectionate, and full of life, with so much potential. He is a big-hearted lad who gives his whole heart, and with the right guidance, he will grow into an incredible companion.

Max has recently been castrated, and while he was feeling (understandably) sorry for himself for a few days after, he was brilliant going into the vets and during his recovery. Although he has had to wear a buster collar just to stop him licking at the area, he doesn't let that bother him and is such a good boy when you take it off to take him out for a walk and pop it back on when he's back in his kennel and he has been so easy to give his pain relief medication to as well, he really has been a model patient. He is such an easy dog to handle, given his size he is no issue at all.

During his recovery period, Max has only been on short walks so that he doesn't overdo it in the play yards, but slowly this past week he has been spending some time in our agility yard to have a run and you can definitely see that he is back to his full, playful self, running around, chasing a tennis ball and being inquisitive about anything and everything.

Max is a fantastic boy, and any time I spend with him is just so enjoyable and full of love and fun, he is such a special dog, I'm constantly scratching my head wondering why and how he's still here.

Where do I start with the wonderful ball of energy that is Max.

First and foremost, the question I ask myself and almost everyone that meets Max asks too, how on earth is he still waiting?! A young, handsome, intelligent dog who is BARRELS of fun. There’s something about Max that is just so loveable and he truly does capture people’s hearts. Many of the volunteers who walk him are always so happy to see him and enjoy their time together.

Recently we’ve been working on nailing a ‘touch’ command. When Max is focused he is such a rewarding dog to train. Sometimes his desire to please takes over and he waves his paw at me until I have to accept it (and of course reward because he's the goodest boy no matter what). He is also learning to be calmer when greeting people and has even had some gentle fuss from some children too. It remains true that Max cannot be homed with children under the age of 16, but it is so important for Max to have positive interactions with respectful children to prevent any reactivity / fear from developing. It also helps teach him to be calm when meeting new people, especially when they’re smaller than him!

Max brings such a unique type of energy to the rescue, he is such a joyful boy and truly comes alive when he is with his people. I threw Max a 1st birthday party and all of his favourite people came throughout the day to play with him and bring him yummy treats, fuss and cuddles. He had the best day and it was so touching to see how loved he is despite not being in a home.

We are doing our very best to raise Max into a well rounded, well socialised and well adjusted adult dog. However, he is at such a crucial stage in his development and has already spent 5 months in kennels. It’s no place for a young dog to grow up. Nearly half of his life spent in kennels patiently waiting for his second chance to come and take him home.

Despite his size Max really is just a baby and definitely a lap dog too. So if you have a spot on the sofa you can share, Max will happily join you and be the bestest friend anyone could wish for.

Myself and Max have formed a very close bond over the last few months we’ve been working together. We take daily walks, go to the big play yard and have plenty of cuddles and fusses.I’m not sure what it is about Max that keeps getting him overlooked, it could be his size or that he is like a big playful puppy or something else, whatever it is, anyone would be lucky to have this handsome chap in their lives, he will always put a smile on your face and he has such a good sense of humour, watching him having zoomies in his kennel yard while he’s jumping off the obstacles in there then stoping then going back round again is nothing short of entertaining, or when he’s fishing treats out of the paddling pool while simultaneously blowing bubbles with his nose.Max truly deserves the world, he is such a sweet and caring boy with a big personality and so much love to give, as well as his big size there is also a big heart and all he wants is to be able to fully give it to someone and finally find his forever home.

Max is a big, happy baby with bags of energy and so much love to give. He is an excitable, affectionate boy who adores attention and loves having people around him. He is always happy to greet you and be part of whatever is going on.

As Max is still young and growing, he is slowly learning his manners and how to greet people politely without jumping. . He will need adopters who can match his energy, continue his training, and give him the stimulation, guidance, and love he needs to thrive.

Max is a gentle, overlooked soul who is learning new things every day at the rescue, but he is missing the comforts of home. He cannot wait to find a family who understands him and can help him blossom into the wonderful companion he is meant to be.With the right home, patience, and plenty of love, Max will make a loyal and joyful best friend.

Since coming back into our care, Max has been working hard on learning how to socialise with other dogs. He absolutely adores them and gets incredibly excited when he sees a potential new friend! Because he’s still young, full of beans, and a bit unaware of his own size, he can sometimes be a little too enthusiastic. This can lead to him becoming overexcited, a bit mouthy, and unintentionally overwhelming other dogs.

To help him learn safe and positive interactions, Max has been socialising while wearing a muzzle. This is purely for his safety and that of other dogs, and his future adopters will need to continue this training and take a responsible approach when introducing him to new canine companions. Aside from that, Max is everything you’d want in a young pup he's bouncy, happy, affectionate, and full of life.

He’s very food oriented, which makes training a dream! He already knows commands like “sit” and has learned great food manners where be waits patiently until he’s told he can eat. Max thrives on mental stimulation and ongoing training, and with the right guidance, he has all the potential to grow into an incredible dog. Max does struggle with separation anxiety and can become destructive if left alone for long periods. He really craves human company so he’ll need a home where someone is around most of the time and is committed to helping him build confidence being alone gradually. He’s such a loving, handsome boy who gives his whole heart, and it would be wonderful to see him back in a home environment where he can truly thrive. As a young pup, he’s missed out on some important early experiences, so a patient, committed family will make all the difference in helping him become the best version of himself.

He is a very excitable, happy boy - essentially an overgrown puppy in a big body. Max is full of fun and enthusiasm and will need an active home that can meet his exercise and stimulation needs. He already knows some basic commands such as “sit”, “paw”, “lay down”, and “wait”, and he is eager to interact with his people.

Max loves other dogs but is often unaware of his size and strength, having grown into such a big lad very quickly. As he is still just a puppy, he is still learning about manners and can be mouthy and plays in a very typical Lurcher way. In his previous home, there was an incident when he was around 3 months old, where he was a little too rough and resulted in a small dog needing veterinary treatment. He has started muzzle training for off-lead play as a precaution, and he will need a home that understands Lurcher play styles and is confident managing this appropriately. We have been socialising him with dogs of all sizes on walks and he is doing very well.

As Max has previously lived in a home, he is familiar with household sights and sounds and is house trained. However, he is still working on his lead manners and can pull when he gets excited. Ongoing training and consistency will be important.

Max will make an amazing addition to a home with experience of similar breeds. He truly is a lovely boy. He is a big-hearted, affectionate lad who is still convinced he can curl up and fit on your lap.

name: Rhea
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teens who respect my space.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have bilateral cataracts & I will be spayed before adoption!

08-11-26 Rhea has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She is a worried little girl who is a little overwhelmed to find herself here at the moment. She can be quite timid when she first meets you, but after a while she does start to come out of her shell and will accept a fuss with a little waggy tail. She is also starting to become quite nosey and inquisitive, which is lovely to see.

Rhea will be looking for a loving home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She currently relies on her kennel friends for comfort and reassurance, so she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to as she begins to find her feet. Rhea does show some signs of resource guarding around food and can grumble at other dogs, so she will need to be fed separately from any other dogs in her new home. This is specifically around sharing food with other dogs, rather than with people. Her adopters will need to be confident in managing this and helping her feel comfortable at mealtimes.

Rhea has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she learns about the routines of home life, including house training and walking on a lead. Having a confident canine companion to show her the ropes will be a big help as she builds her confidence and starts to discover the world outside the rescue.

Rhea could share her home with dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over, who can appreciate and understand that she will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and her own space to settle in.

Rhea is a sweet, timid girl who will need a little extra time, kindness and reassurance to help her find her paws. With the right home and a lovely doggy friend by her side, we hope she will gradually grow in confidence and learn to enjoy all the comforts of home life.

Rhea has arrived with bilateral cataracts, which does not seem to be bothering her at this time but will need to be monitored in her future home.

Rhea has been given the Gift of Life by Rosalind Steven

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Benji
description:
I could live with older, dog-savvy teens who respect my space.

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I have never met cats.

I'd like a secure garden to have fun playtimes in.

I walk on a lead and would enjoy a nice walk once a day.

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

03-11-26 Benji is a beautiful, playful boy who originally came into our care as an unclaimed dog in 2024. He was adopted but has sadly returned to us because of illness in the family, meaning his owners were no longer able to care for him.

Benji is feeling a little out of sorts being back in kennels but is coping well. He is a super-loving boy who absolutely adores attention, cuddles and bum scratches. He has been spending lots of time in the office with us while his exercise is restricted and is always happy to soak up some fuss. He has lots of character and a wonderfully silly personality, and we know he would love nothing more than to be back in a home where he can relax on the sofa and enjoy life with his favourite people!

Benji can be a little reactive towards other dogs when out on walks, but having spent time in a home, he has made some lovely improvements. He is currently kennelled with a friend and we feel he could potentially live with another suitable dog or as an only dog. His adopters will need to be understanding of his needs and willing to continue supporting him with his training around other dogs. When Benji was initially with us, he could snap at feet when leaving his kennel, but this behaviour has improved massively since his time in a home. He is generally much better around doorways, although he can still become uncomfortable if someone lingers in a doorway or enters without greeting him, so his adopters will need to be mindful of this.

Having lived in a home before, Benji is familiar with the sights and sounds of everyday life and will hopefully settle back into a home routine with a little time. He needs a calm home with adopters who understand his breed and can give him the consistency and reassurance he needs. He can live with teenagers aged 16 and over who understand his needs and will respect his space.

Benji was castrated and had nasal wedge surgery in 2024. He can still experience episodes of being sick, particularly following exercise, excitement or periods of stress. He is currently being trialled on a course of medication to see whether this helps manage his symptoms, but he may require further investigation and potentially additional surgery to address his breathing, such as BOAS surgery, in the future. His exercise and activity levels are currently being managed, so he will need adopters who are happy to accommodate his reduced exercise needs and understand that he may require further veterinary treatment and monitoring as needed.

Benji really is a lovely little man who is full of character and has so much love to give. He is a typical silly Frenchie who is desperate to get back to being the couch potato he deserves to be! With a calm home, understanding adopters and plenty of cuddles, we know he will be so happy to have a sofa to call his own again.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Royal
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I would like to live with a female dog. No cats please!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can walk on a lead and harness and love to explore quiet areas.

I am learning about house training in my foster home, and am doing so good!

Royal is a very special Chow Chow who has come to us from a breeder in search of his forever home. When he first arrived, he was extremely frightened of the world around him and was very wary of being touched or handled. Thanks to gentle care and patience, Royal has made incredible progress and is continuing to blossom in foster, where he is experiencing home life for the very first time.

Royal has exceeded all expectations with how well he has settled into foster. He has been an absolute superstar, sleeping soundly through the night, travelling well in the car, walking beautifully on lead and has even been completely clean in the house. Every day brings a new milestone, and it has been a joy to watch his confidence grow as he discovers all the comforts and pleasures of family life.

Although Royal is still nervous of people initially, he so desperately wants to trust and tries his hardest to be brave. He has begun asking his foster carers for gentle neck and bum scratches, happily takes treats from their hands, enjoys rummaging through the toy box, has found his little voice and now greets them with his wonderful wagging tail. He is such a sweet, gentle soul who simply needs time to work things out at his own pace.

Royal absolutely relies on the resident female dogs in foster for confidence and reassurance. He watches their every move, learning how to be part of a family, and loves playing alongside them. He will need to share his forever home with at least one kind, confident female dog who enjoys a good play and can continue to show him the way. He cannot live with cats.

As this is Royal's first experience of living in a home, he thrives on routine and will need patient, understanding adopters who will allow him to settle without pressure. He has made remarkable progress already, but he is still very nervous of the unknown and benefits from people who understand that he needs time to process new experiences. A calm, rural or quiet home would suit him best, as he is currently worried by traffic. He is looking for an adult-only home with breed experience and experience with very nervous rescue dogs would be highly beneficial.

Royal has recently had a bath and full groom at the rescue and was an absolute gentleman throughout. As a Chow Chow, his beautiful coat will require regular daily grooming. He is very tolerant of being brushed when it is introduced slowly, little and often, and this has become an important part of his routine.

Royal is an incredibly special boy who has embraced this new chapter in his life with quiet bravery. With patience, kindness and the continued support of confident canine companions, he will become a wonderfully loyal and loving companion. Watching him continue to discover the world and grow in confidence will be an incredibly rewarding journey, and he is sure to make his forever family smile every single day.

Royal is currently being treated for an ear infection.

Wow! This darling boy has just exceeded all expectations with how well he’s settled into his very first home, in his first week. Not a single accident (unheard of for a boy), sleeps soundly over night out of a crate, happy to be left alone with the company of the resident dogs, walks well on a lead, travels well. A literal angel boy.

Royal is the sweetest soul, he doesn’t trust humans easily but he really wants to and tries so hard to be brave.

He relies heavily on our resident girl gang for confidence & reassurance, watching & copying them intently to learn what being a member of a family is all about.

After an initial overwhelming few days for him, every day now brings a new ‘first’ & burst of joy on our part! Asking for a neck / bum scratch, taking a treat from our hand, rummaging in the toy box, playing with the girls, finding his little voice & wagging his amazing tail when we talk to him. He is just loving this next step in life and is so ready to be someone’s special boy.

Royal currently needs an adult only home as has not yet been tested with children. He needs confident kind resident female dogs who like a good play. A rural / quiet location would be preferable as he’s currently quite scared of traffic.

He is still very nervous of the unknown, thrives on routine and needs to be guided and given time to work things out without any pressure so experience with very scared dogs would be helpful.

As a Chow, his beautiful coat will need grooming daily. He is very tolerant of this if done slowly, little & often.

Please get in touch if you feel you might be the right match for this special big guy, he will make you smile every day.

Royal is not a dog I’ve had the chance to work with until recently. I’ve heard a lot about him, as he’s one of our longer stayers. I had heard many great things from other members of staff, including the incredible progress he’s made since joining us!When I did get the chance to work with him, my first impression was “oh my days, you are beautiful!” On first sight, he is one of the most beautiful dogs I’ve ever seen and certainly the most stunning chow I’ve ever seen! How can you look at this handsome boy and not fall in love?!When I actually began working with him, I realised how shy and timid he actually was. Initially, he wouldn’t come to the front of the kennel to see me, he’d hide away in the back. It was evident to me that this boy did not trust me. As I continued to work with him, I was very aware of my actions, to ensure I wasn’t causing any anxiety. I began with treats (who doesn’t love a cheeky bribe?). It slowly worked. Initially, he wanted nothing to do with me. I didn’t want to invade his safe spaces (safe spaces are so important for a more scared or anxious dog. Could you imagine a big scary stranger coming into your home and not leaving? I wouldn’t feel too easy if that occurred to me). So, I’d place the treat and leave the kennel. He’d come out, have a little nosey and take the treat. With time, he began slowly coming out of the back as I entered his kennel. He then began taking treats from my hands and now, whenever I walk onto the section, he comes straight to the gate and waits for me. Honestly, such an incredible feeling making a bond like this with such an incredible boy! There is honestly no feeling like it. They say a dog is a humans best friend but, what no one tells you it works both ways. To build that bond, teach him that I’m not scary, I’m here to help him feel safe, comfortable, happy and to get such a response… it’s honestly the best feeling in the world. Royal needs a home, he needs people to show him this on a day to day basis. We do what we can but, we can’t teach him the safety and comfort of a home, of a family that’s there for him 24/7.Once I got to know this guy a little more, I was taken away. We go out on walks. I feel like this was another bonding experience for us. He loves a walk but, loud noises and interactions with loud people/dogs do freak him out, thus we try to go for quieter walks. He also loves frolicking in the yard. From my experience, he seems to just love being outside!When I worked with him, he didn’t have a friend in his kennel, however, since working with him I have seen him enjoying in the yard with other dogs and is now kennelled with a boxer. He seems very happy. As previously mentioned on his profile, he is to be homed with females around his size or alone. I have not worked with him enough to comment further on his compatibility and amiability with other dogs so, please read the rest of his profile and updates to get a fuller understanding of this incredible boy!At this point, I’ve worked with him enough for him to trust me. He’s happy to see me, he’s fine for me to touch him and fuss him. The Royal I see is a happy dude. He is a scared dog, I’m very aware of that but, the Royal I know now is far different to the Royal I first met. You just have to gain his trust and he’ll let you see him. When you first meet him, he will be shy. He’ll hide and he will not trust you. DO NOT let this deter you. He is one of the sweetest dogs I’ve ever met. From when I first met him to now, I feel like he’s a completely different dog. I was respectful of his boundaries, slow and calm, I did what I could to make him feel comfortable and safe, he then began to trust me and show me his true self (he hides it beneath all that fur). Honestly, I love him. I will take time out of my day to go see him, give him a little treat and some love, just because he is honestly that special. I cannot believe he’s been here over a year. He is one of our most special dogs. I don’t see how anyone can get to know this dog and not love him.Don’t overlook this fluffy dude. Yes, he’s shy and nervous but, the longer you spend with him, care for him and gain his trust, the more you’ll fall in love with him. I can say with confidence; if you put the effort in with Royal, you will fall in love with him.

I absolutely love this boy with my whole heart.

I've been working hard on helping him get used to being brushed because, as a Chow, it's something his future adopters will need to keep up with regularly to keep his coat healthy and prevent mats from developing, especially behind his ears.

Royal is now an absolute angel when it comes to grooming. I brush him every day, and with it being shedding season, no matter how long I brush for, there always seems to be more fur coming out! These days, he simply finds a comfy spot, settles down, and lets me get on with it. If he's had enough, or if I come across a mat that's uncomfortable for him, he communicates so well to let me know he's done for the day.

I also recently decided it was time to give him a bath. I wasn't sure how he'd cope, as it involved picking him up and putting him in the bath, but he was an absolute angel from start to finish. He allowed me to pick him up without any fuss and stood beautifully while I bathed and shampooed him.

I'm so incredibly proud of him. Afterwards, I introduced him to the grooming blower to help remove some of his loose coat. He wasn't a huge fan of it, but he tolerated it for a short while, and I'll continue using it regularly so he can build his confidence with it.

I honestly think all this grooming time has strengthened our bond even more, because lately he seems to be seeking out so much more affection and attention from me. He's such a special boy, and it has been wonderful watching his confidence grow.

Royal has now been with us for over a year, and we’re still waiting for the right person to see just how special he is. He’s had two meet and greets during this time, but sadly neither worked out as he was too nervous meeting new families.

Royal is a sensitive boy who simply needs time, patience, and understanding. He can be unsure at first, but once he begins to trust you, his cheeky, affectionate personality really shines through and it’s such a joy to see.

With a consistent routine, Royal truly thrives. He now enjoys running freely around our large yard without a harness or lead, and when it’s time to go back, he comes straight over. He’s also been out on two longer walks away from the rescue with one of our regular volunteers and has done amazingly well.

All Royal is looking for is someone willing to give him the time and patience he deserves. In return, he’ll become a loyal and loving companion.

I’ve come on leaps and bounds over the past month. I’m still a little shy and can get nervous when I meet new people, but I’m working on it!

I feel most comfortable when I spend quality time with people. It doesn’t take long for me to start feeling at ease (though I still sometimes like my own space). The more time you spend with me, the more comfortable I become—and treats help too! I’ll return your love in equal measure, as long as I’m given the right time, support, and respect.

I love going out for walks, though I can get nervous around loud noises or sudden movements. They might make me jump or feel uneasy, but a bit of love and reassurance always helps!

I feel more comfortable every day. I benefit not only from interaction with my humans, but also from the company of my kennel friends that I live with.

Another month has gone by, and my cheeky boy Royal is still waiting in kennels. I honestly don’t know why this handsome lad isn’t getting much interest. Not only is he completely unique-looking, but he also has the funniest, quirkiest personality. If you want a dog who’ll make you laugh every single day here he is!

Royal is 99% kennel clean and always keeps his bedding tidy… well, until I make his bed perfectly for him. Then he likes to “show me how it’s supposed to be done” by pulling it all across the floor. He walks beautifully on the lead now; he can still get a little spooked from time to time, but he’s made massive progress since the day he arrived.

He loves his toys he just doesn’t love sharing them! He’s also a bit selective with kennel mates, so his ideal home would include a calm, placid large female dog who won’t make too much fuss over him.

Royal truly is an amazing boy, inside and out, and I hope he doesn’t have to wait much longer for the forever home he deserves.

Royal never fails to make us smile with his crazy, funny, and quirky personality. He’s got such a cheeky side to him just waiting for the right people to help it shine.

On the lead, Royal is already walking beautifully, though he can still get a little nervous at times. His new family will need to be patient and willing to help him build confidence. Loud noises or sudden movements can overwhelm him, so he’ll do best with calm, quiet walks to start.

This week Royal had his very first trip down to the big yard! He loved it, though he found his confidence by sticking close to his doggy friend. With more practice, we’re sure he’ll begin to explore on his own.

Royal absolutely adores other dogs. Once he’s settled in, he loves to play, so he’ll need a kind and confident resident dog to show him the ropes, give him reassurance, and of course, enjoy plenty of playtime together.

He’s such a handsome boy with so much love to give we can’t believe he hasn’t found his forever home yet!

This past month has been a huge step forward for our boy Royal! Once a little unsure of the world, Royal is now walking beautifully on lead, it’s such a massive step for him considering how nervous he once was!

Royal currently shares his kennel with both a male and a female dog and he’s proving to be a respectful and easy companion. He enjoys their company, often watching what they do and following their lead. Royal will definitely need another resident dog around his size in his home, so he can continue to have the doggy companionship to help him continue to grow in confidence.

Despite his progress, Royal is still a sensitive soul, and it takes a little time for him to warm up to you. Royals forever family will need to give him time and patience to come out of his shell, so for this reason I believe Royal would be best suited to a home with no children.

Please don’t leave Royal waiting much longer for his forever home, he really deserves a cosy sofa to curl up on!

I’m so proud of Royal, this boy has come on tremendously since arriving at Many Tears. From arriving a terrified dog and very unsure of us humans, he has now slowly but surely begun to trust us and realise we are not so bad, especially when we arrive with cheesy treats.

Royal loves food, toys and being outside in our yards. He has just began harness training, ready to begin lead walking. At the moment he is not so keen on lead walking but he has taken a few tentative steps and with the help of some squeezy cheese and possibly a confident doggie friend to follow I think it won’t be long before he can begin to enjoy exploring the world.

Royals adopters will need to understand he is still very wary and unsure of his environment and he is going to need plenty of time, love and patience to trust his humans, but in the right home and given time I think this boy is going to be a big, playful and lovable boy. Royal will need a home where there is already a resident dog.

Royal is a very scared boy who has come to us from a breeder. He is especially scared when it comes to being touched by us humans but when you get him in the back of the kennel he will allow you to gently stroke him but he is uncomfortable with this. At the moment Royal could possibly make the wrong decision if handled incorrectly but this is purely through fear and he is already starting to make improvements. He will actually get excited to see his kennel mum in the mornings and will wag his tail but he’s not sure how to interact with her yet.

Royal has never lived in a home so this is going to be completely overwhelming at first and he will definitely need at least one other dog in the home to help his confidence. This will help him with house training and lead walking but these are things that are going to take him time to learn as the garden may be as scary as the home at first.

Royal will need a very calm and quiet, adult only home and adopters who have lots of experience with scared dogs. We think he’ll come out of his shell a lot more over time but Royal needs a lot of TLC, time and patience.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Dutch
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who respect my space.

I need to be the only dog in my new home. No cats please!

I walk well on a lead and muzzle trained. I would enjoy an active lifestyle!

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I am already vaccinated and neutered and ready for my new home!

Dutch is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a pound in Ireland in search of a fresh start. Unfortunately, we don't know much about his history, but what we do know is that he is one of the most loving and affectionate dogs you could ever hope to meet, with a heart as big as his personality. Dutch simply wants to be close to his people, whether that's following you around, leaning into you for fuss, or curling up beside you for cuddles. Being with the people he loves is all he really wants.

Dutch would love to find a home with adopters who are around for most of the day and can include him in everyday life. He thrives on human companionship and will make a wonderfully devoted shadow to his new family. He will need adopters who have experience with similar breeds and understand typical breed traits, including prey drive and the need for appropriate mental and physical enrichment.

Dutch would be best suited to life as an only dog. Although he can socialise well with other dogs of a similar size, he can become overexcited and mouthy, which may lead to frustration. Because of this, he is muzzle trained and wears a muzzle during social interactions to help him continue building positive experiences. He cannot live with cats or small furries.

As Dutch has never lived in a home before, he will need support with house training and learning the general routines of family life. He is such a clever boy and always tries his very best to do the right thing, so we are confident he will enjoy learning with patient, positive guidance.

Dutch already walks well on a lead, although he can occasionally be reactive when passing other kennels. This is understandable in a busy rescue environment and may be something his adopters will need to continue working on. He is an energetic, happy-go-lucky boy who is more than ready to start exploring the world with his new family. An active home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, enrichment, training and quality time with his people would suit him perfectly.

Dutch could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate that he will need a gentle introduction to his new surroundings and his own space to settle in.

Dutch is bright, affectionate and full of love. He has so much to offer and is simply looking for someone to love as much as he loves them. For the right family, he will be an incredibly loyal, fun-loving and devoted companion.

Dutch has a passport and travel document.

Dutch has been given the Gift of Life by Louise Southward

I’m truly so sad that Dutch is still waiting for his forever home. It’s such a shame that certain breeds can be so easily overlooked.

Dutch is the most sweet, loving, loyal and clever boy. He absolutely loves everyone, has bags of confidence and is always bursting with excitement to say hello to everyone he meets out on a walk.

We've recently started walking Dutch with different friends each day to help him learn to manage some of his reactivity, and honestly, after just one walk, the very next day he was absolutely brilliant!

Dutch isn't reactive because he wants to be difficult, he's simply so excited and eager to say hello that he's still learning how to manage those feelings.

He's such a smart boy and has picked things up so quickly. He just needs someone who will keep that clever brain busy, give him some guidance and help him continue to learn.

Please don't overlook Dutch. There is so much to love about this boy, and we would love nothing more than to see him finally find his forever home.

I still can’t quite understand how this incredibly smart and loving boy hasn’t found his forever home yet.If you’re looking for a dog to train, learn new tricks and go on lots of adventures with, then Dutch really is your boy.He’s the best of both worlds a crazy, energetic boy who also absolutely loves his people and loves nothing more than a good snuggle.

Dutch, or as I like to call him, Dutchy, is honestly one of the most loving and affectionate boys you could ever hope to meet.

He's the kind of dog who just wants to be close to you. Whether it's following you around, leaning into you for fuss, or curling up for cuddles, being with his people is all he really wants. Watching him have to go back into his kennel after spending time together is heartbreaking because kennel life is just no place for a boy like him.

What makes it even sadder is that he hasn't received a single application. If I'm honest, my biggest worry is that he'll become one of our long-stay dogs, and my heart breaks at the thought of that because he simply doesn't deserve it.

He's such a clever boy and always tries so hard to do the right thing. He recently went on his first long walk with one of our wonderful regular volunteers and was an absolute angel. He took everything in his stride and made everyone so proud.

He's also been having play dates with our lovely girl, Swanny, to help him burn off some of that doggy energy while learning good doggy manners.

At the end of the day, Dutchy is just a baby. He's got the biggest heart, so much love to give, and he deserves a home where he'll be someone's whole world instead of waiting behind kennel doors. I know his family is out there somewhere; I just hope they find him before he spends another day wondering why no one has chosen him.

Dutch is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a pound in Ireland in search of a fresh start. Unfortunately, we don't know much about his history, but what we do know is that he is one of the most loving and affectionate dogs you could ever hope to meet.

He would love to find a loving home with adopters who are around most of the time and would have plenty of time to spend with him. He would need adopters who have experience with similar breeds and experience with his typical breed traits like prey drive etc.

Dutch would be best suited to being homed as an only dog as although he does socialise well with other dogs of his size, he can become over excited and mouthy which can lead to frustration. For this reason he is being trained to wear a muzzle when socialising. He cannot be homed with cats or small furries.

As Dutch has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. With patience and guidance, we think he will adapt well and enjoy all the comforts a home has to offer.

Dutch can already walk well on a lead, though he can be a little reactive when passing other kennels, this is understandable in a busy rescue environment, but may be something his adopters will need to work with him on. He is an energetic and incredibly lovely bo who ie is happy-go-lucky in nature and is more than ready to start adventuring with his new adopters. He would love an active home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, enrichment, and quality time with his people.

Dutch could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate and understand that he will need a gentle and quiet introduction to the home, along with his own space to settle in.

He is a bright, affectionate, and fun-loving boy who is sure to make a wonderful and loyal companion for a lucky family.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

name: Archie
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

I have been neutered and have had 21 teeth removed.

Archie is such a sweet little man who came into our care from a breeder. He was adopted but has sadly been returned after his adopters felt they were not the right match for him. Archie formed a very strong bond with his female owner, but found it much harder to build a relationship with her husband, who was frequently away from home and therefore had very little opportunity to gain Archie's trust. When Archie becomes closely bonded to his favourite person, he can become protective of them. In his previous home, he nipped when he was sitting with his owner and her husband approached, so his new adopters will need to understand this behaviour and be prepared to continue building his confidence in a positive and patient way.

He is a cuddly and affectionate little dog once he feels comfortable, although he isn't quite brave enough to take treats from our hands just yet. Although Archie gets on well with other dogs, he can become protective of his favourite person around them, so we think he would be happiest as the only dog in the home, where he can relax and build a close bond with his new family.

As Archie has lived in a home before, he will already be familiar with the sights and sounds of home life. However, he may need a little reminding of his house training in a new environment. He walks well on a lead and enjoys his walks with volunteers.

Archie is looking for a quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of the breed and of rescue dogs. He will need people who are happy to give him the time and space he needs to settle and understand that he is safe.

Archie is doing really well since returning to us and his confidence is growing all the time. He is such a loving little dog, and in the right home, we hope he will continue to thrive and become a devoted companion.

We absolutely love this little guy at the rescue, Archie may be small but his personality is mighty. He is funny, lovable and impossible not to love. Archie is still a tiny bit shy with new people but it’s taking him less and less time to open up to new people and dogs. Archie loves to play with tennis balls, smother you with kisses and generally amuse us with his cheeky personality. Archie would like a child-free home as he is still a little anxious at times.

Archie is an absolute pleasure to work with! It’s been some time now, and our bond continues to grow stronger every day.He absolutely loves smothering you with kisses and will do anything to get himself onto your lap! Archie has been kennelled with a few dogs and socialised with plenty more, but he has become particularly taken with a Cocker called Trixie. They share some similar traits, including not wanting to share their humans, although neither has displayed any jealousy towardsthe other so far. They absolutely love running laps around the yard together before heading straight into your lap for some fuss. Archie will even stand on Trixie’s back just to make sure he gets in on the action and doesn’t miss out on any attention!As mentioned, Archie is yet to display any jealous traits towards either dogs or humans, but that doesn’t mean he won’t potentially show this once settled into a home. It’s something any potential adopter should be mindful of and prepared to manage appropriately.

What I can promise, though, is that Archie will become your best friend. He has so much love to give and, once he trusts you, he will love you unconditionally.This gorgeous boy deserves someone who will give him the love, patience and understanding he needs — and in return, you’ll have a loyal companion who will want nothing more than to be by your side.

Archie is the funniest and cheekiest of little Dachshunds. Archie needs a little time to warm to you (but not all that long), and once he does, he is the most lovely of boys. I have been caring for him for a few weeks now, and I am totally smitten.

Archie walks beautifully on lead and loves nothing more than when we venture out for a stroll along the lanes around the rescue. Archie is very fond of his toys and will happily run around the yard with a ball in his mouth. He will also spend much time organising his cuddly toys, making sure they are in just the right place.

Archie has been kennelled with other small female dogs. He seems to do best with robust smaller females, as he can be a little frisky with the more timid dogs. Archie could go as an only dog in the right home, one where there are humans who will have lots of time for him.

Archie is very enthusiastic with his kisses once he knows you and will desperately clamber over you for fusses. Archie is an all-round lovely little dog, best suited to a quiet adult home where there is plenty of love, time, and patience for him to truly settle in.

Archie is such a sweet little man who came into our care from a breeder. He was adopted but has sadly been returned after his adopters felt they were not the right match for him. Archie formed a very strong bond with his female owner, but found it much harder to build a relationship with her husband, who was frequently away from home and therefore had very little opportunity to gain Archie's trust. When Archie becomes closely bonded to his favourite person, he can become protective of them. In his previous home, he nipped when he was sitting with his owner and her husband approached, so his new adopters will need to understand this behaviour and be prepared to continue building his confidence in a positive, patient way.

He is a cuddly, affectionate little dog once he feels comfortable, although he isn't quite brave enough to take treats from our hands just yet. Although Archie gets on well with other dogs, he can become protective of his favourite person around them, so we think he would be happiest as the only dog in the home, where he can relax and build a close bond with his new family.

Archie is a gorgeous little boy who came to us from a breeder and was understandably unsure of the world around him. It was truly heartbreaking to see how frightened he was as he would shy away from human contact and retreat when approached. Archie needs gentle handling, patience, and calm, slow movements to help him feel safe. Already, we are seeing progress. He enjoys a gentle fuss and has grown some confidence wagging his tail enthusiastically.

He gains reassurance from other dogs and will need a kind, confident resident dog in his new home to help guide him, boost his confidence, and show him that people and home life can be safe and rewarding.

Archie has never lived in a home before, so his adopters will need to be patient and understanding as he learns the basics, including house training and walking on a lead. He could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over, who can appreciate and understand that he will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and his own space to settle in.

Since arriving with us, Archie has undergone extensive and much-needed dental treatment and has had 21 teeth removed. He is now recovering well and feeling much more comfortable.

name: Pippa
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need an extra secure garden to keep me safe.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

30-09-26 Pippa is a very scared and nervous lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is very worried about being handled and becomes stressed if we attempt to pick her up. She will try to jump from our arms and, because of this, we would consider her a flight risk and she will need fencing of at least 6ft in her new garden to keep her safe. She will need very careful handling and adopters who understand just how frightened she is at the moment.

Pippa gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Pippa has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be very patient and give her time to adjust to all the new sights, sounds and experiences that come with living in a home.

Pippa will need a quiet, confident, adult-only home where she can relax and settle into her new surroundings without too much hustle and bustle. Her adopters will need to have ex-breeding experience and understand her nervous nature and allow her to progress at her own pace.

Pippa is a very worried girl right now, but with the security of a kind canine companion and a calm, patient family, we hope she will slowly begin to feel safe and gain the confidence she needs to enjoy her new life.

Pippa has been given the Gift of Life by Margaret Hunter

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. name: Milo
description:
I will need an adult-only home that understands me.

I will need to be the only dog in my new home, so all of the attention is on me!

I will need an extra secure garden, at least 6ft+ where I will be safe!

I walk well on a lead but will need my adopters to be understanding of my needs!

I have lived in a home before so may I may already know the basics.

I will be neutered before finding my forever home!

06-10-26 Milo is a super sweet boy who has come to us from a home through no fault of his own. Sadly, he has already been through more changes than a young dog should have to, and he is understandably a little worried in new environments. He takes a lot of comfort from people he knows, but once he feels comfortable, his fun and affectionate personality really starts to shine.

Milo is an incredibly sweet boy who absolutely loves being close to his people and thinks he is the perfect lap dog! He is happiest when he can have a cuddle and will happily climb up for a lap sit. He is a sensitive little soul and will need a kind and patient home where he can continue to build his confidence and learn that he is safe and secure.

Milo will be looking for a home where he can be the only dog and get all the fuss and attention for himself. We are told that he has had a previous incident with a cat and so he cannot be homed with cats or small furries and must be kept on lead unless in a secure area.

Milo has missed out on some socialisation, but he is currently working on his social skills and is making lovely progress. He can happily walk alongside calm dogs and has had some nice greetings. He doesn't always know what to make of other dogs yet and can sometimes get a little carried away when mixing, but with continued positive socialisation we are sure his confidence will grow. He can also react if another dog barks at him first while on lead, so his new family will need to understand this and help him learn how to navigate these situations.

Milo will need an adult-only home with people who have experience of bull breeds and understand what sensitive souls they can be.Although he is a wonderful boy, he would not be suitable for a first time dog owner.He will need a kind and patient family who can give him time to settle and continue building his confidence. He will also need the time he is left home alone built up gradually as he settles into his new home.

Milo will need an extra secure garden of at least 6ft to keep him safe, as he is a young and active boy who could be an escape artist if given the opportunity.

Milo is such a lovely young boy who has already been through so much change. With the right family, patience and continued socialisation, we know he will make a wonderful companion and be the loving, fun little lap dog he is so desperate to be.

name: Moxy
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult-only home.

I will need a kind, calm resident dog to show me the ropes. I'm unsure of cats.

I would like an extra-secure garden to spend time in.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I am currently in a foster home where I am learning about home life!

Moxy is a worried little girl who has come to us from a breeder and is now in foster, where she is beginning to show her lovely, affectionate personality. She can be unsure around new people, but as she learns to trust you, more of her sweet nature shines through. In the evenings, she will come to her fosterers for a cuddle on her own terms, which is lovely to see as she continues to grow in confidence.

Moxy will need an adult-only home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and understand that she needs time, patience and kindness to settle into her new life. A calm, quiet environment with minimal disruption will be important, as will having a gentle, quiet resident dog to help her feel safe and guide her through home life. Moxy has struggled with a more vocal dog in her foster home, so her canine companion will need to be calm and considerate of her needs.

Moxy has never lived in a home before and is learning about house training and everyday routines in foster. Her new family will need to continue this patiently and gently introduce her to lead walking. She has shown signs of digging, so she will also need an extra-secure garden to keep her safe.

Moxy arrived with sore eyes, and our vet noted that her lower eyelid is irregular, although this is not currently causing her any issues. We are also concerned that her vision is significantly reduced, as her depth perception seems affected. She may bump into things or be startled when other dogs approach unexpectedly, so her adopters will need to understand her visual difficulties and help her navigate her surroundings safely. She also arrived with sore skin and old concrete sores, which we hope will continue to improve.

Moxy has already made lovely progress and is gradually learning to trust the people around her. She will need a special family who can offer a peaceful home, a calm canine companion and the understanding she needs to feel secure. With time, patience and gentle reassurance, we hope this affectionate little girl will continue to blossom and discover just how lovely life can be.

Moxy has been on our section for a few weeks now & she is such a delight to be around.

Dependent on where Moxy is will decide which side of Moxy you will get. Both sides are a truly beautiful dog, but one is incredibly sad & shut down and the other is a wonderful, affectionate girl who truly tries her hardest to be brave.

When in the kennel you’ll find Moxy in the back, she’ll appear sad, broken & totally overwhelmed. She tries to dig a lot, and burrow herself behind any beds she can find. We have swapped these beds out with a big comfy duvet now where she likes to chill in the corner. However I do think she sees it as her safe space, where she will hide from the outside world. Once she’s out of that kennel, and running to the yard she will wag her body in its entirety as she greets other kennels desperately trying to make new friends.

Even in the yard, Moxy can still feel overwhelmed and will sit in the corner & dig at times, and we’ve even tried taking her out on a harness but she remains frozen. But once she’s comfortable in the company she is around, she is the most affectionate girl. She happily sits next to you, gives you kisses and that tail really does not stop wagging. Her company is joyous, and being one of her trusted people is so incredibly rewarding, and brightens every day I spend with her.

Moxy’s people will need to take it easy with her, need to understand exbreeders, and be patient & kind along her journey at home. Mixing her nervous character along with her poor eyesight, being at home is likely to be very scary for her. As one of her kennel mummies, I can vouch for her & tell you that gaining her trust, and gaining her as a family member will be the most fulfilling experience, and one I am extremely jealous of. Moxy deserves love, care & a place to feel safe after all this time feeling scared & overwhelmed.

Moxy, like a lot of ex breeder dogs, is a very nervous dog. When I first met her, she wouldn’t leave the back, didn’t want me to get near her and I had to carry her back and forth from the yard. On my second day with Moxy, she ran straight to the yard as I opened her kennel door and, once I entered the yard, she was jumping all over me, kissing me, genuinely thrilled to see me. This is behaviour that truly shocked me in the best possible way.

It’s now been a couple of weeks since I first worked with her and the affection she shows me and the confidence she found has only grown. She’s truly incredible.Around new people, she reverts back to shutting down and hiding in the back. Despite this, we still have an incredible relationship. Moxy needs to be shown she can trust you.

Once this girl trusts you, you’ll see the same side I see. You won’t see this side if you met her on a show around of our kennels or even if you were let in her kennel to socialise her. This is something you can only experience from adopting her and progressing her like we do. I truly love her with all my heart. Take a chance on her and I have no doubts you’ll experience the same as I.

Moxy is a very worried little girl who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She is feeling quite overwhelmed to find herself here at the moment and is in need of lots of TLC, patience and reassurance. Once she gets to know you, she does start to come out of her shell and then enjoys a gentle fuss.

Moxy will need a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need plenty of time to settle in at her own pace. She will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help her learn how wonderful her life can be now. We would consider homing her with old, dog savvy teenagers.

Moxy has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her. Her new family will need to be kind and understanding as she learns all about home life, including new skills like house training and walking on a lead. She will need gentle encouragement and understanding as she settles in.

Moxy is a very sweet girl who has had a difficult start in life. She now needs someone who will give her the time, patience and love she needs to blossom. With a kind canine friend by her side and a quiet, understanding home, we hope she will slowly gain confidence and discover how lovely life can be.

Moxy has arrived with slightly sore eyes and our vet has noted her low eyelid is irregular but doesn't feel this is causing her any issues at the moment, but will need to be monitored moving forwards. Although she can see, her vision isn't the best, but she doesn't let this slow her down and gets around well. She also arrived with sore skin and old concrete sores, which will hopefully feel much better soon.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Ursula
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can now walk on a lead and harness, but need more practice.

I am learning about house training in my foster home, but will need more training.

I have a bilateral Grade 2 patella luxation.

Ursula is a sweet little lady who has come into our care from a breeder and is now enjoying life in a foster home, where she has been starting to experience home life for the first time ever. She is still slowly coming out of her shell and can easily become overwhelmed by new situations, but overall she is a very gentle girl who is making steady progress. When she does become worried, she can panic and may choose to make the wrong decision purely out of fear. On occasion, she has nipped when frightened, so she will need understanding adopters who can recognise when she is feeling overwhelmed and give her the gentle support she needs.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have experience of scared ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace.

Ursula takes comfort from having a kind and confident dog around her and will need a resident dog in her new home who can help her understand that new things are not always scary. She would benefit greatly from having a canine companion to look to for reassurance as she continues to settle and build her confidence. With the right support, we are sure Ursula will continue to become more comfortable and show her lovely personality.

Ursula had never lived in a home before moving to her wonderful foster home, but she is already doing wonderfully with her house training in her foster home. She happily sleeps through the night without any accidents and is essentially house trained, which is fantastic progress. Her adopters will still need to be patient and understanding as she continues to learn about home life and build her confidence.

She has started learning to walk on a lead and harness and though she still needs more practice to build up her confidence, she is doing well.

Ursula was underweight when she arrived but is gradually gaining weight and becoming healthier and stronger. She is a gentle little girl who needs a calm and understanding home where she can continue to build her confidence at her own pace. She may still become overwhelmed from time to time, but she is learning that she is safe and that her people will be there to reassure her.

Ursula has bilateral Grade 2 luxating patellas, but with gentle exercise this is currently not causing her any problems. Her adopters will need to be aware that this is a pre-existing condition and a disclaimer will apply, meaning it would not be covered by insurance. She also arrived with an umbilical hernia, which has since been repaired during her spay.

Ursula is a sweet and gentle little girl who has already made some lovely progress during her time in foster. She will need a family who can offer her patience, kindness and plenty of reassurance as she continues to find her confidence. With a kind resident dog by her side and a calm, loving home, we are sure Ursula will blossom into a wonderful companion.

Ursula has been given the Gift of Life by Anne Breen

Ursula has now had an amazing groom and looks like the poodle she is. So far Ursula has had no interest at all and I don’t understand why.

This baby is only 3 but has already seen things she struggles to forget. She’s only now understanding that hands can mean treats or gentle strokes and are nothing to worry about.

She’s now out walking with her doggy friends and loves all those smells. She is still nervous when someone approaches but I’m sure that will slowly pass once she realises they only want to say hello.

Ursula does easily panic and when this happens she doesn’t always make the right decision but with a calm voice and gentle hands she calms down.

She so deserves a calm and gentle household and relies on my resident dogs. So will require a friendly resident dog in her forever home.

Ursula has now been in foster for just over a fortnight and is still slowly coming out of her shell. She’s a very gentle girl but can easily get overwhelmed. When this happens she does tend to make the wrong decisions, but calms down fairly quickly.

She is gradually increasing her weight as she was underweight when she arrived.

Ursula will need a kind and gentle resident dog to help her understand new things are not always bad. Ursula happily sleeps through the night without any accidents and basically house trained. She has been diagnosed with grade 2 luxating patellas but with gentle exercise it’s not causing her any problems. She will have a disclaimer for this problem.

Ursula is a sweet little lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is confident enough to come over and greet you when you approach, but she can lose confidence when it comes to being handled and may retreat until she feels safe again. With patience and gentle reassurance, she is continuing to grow in confidence every day.Ursula could be the only dog in a home, provided her adopters have plenty of time to help build her confidence and support her as she settles into family life. She could also happily live with a kind and confident resident dog who she can look to for reassurance as she learns about home life and continues to gain confidence.Having never lived in a home before, Ursula will need patient and understanding adopters to help her with house training and lead walking and all the new experiences that come with family life.Ursula is a gentle, affectionate little lady who simply needs a family willing to give her the time she deserves. With kindness, patience, and understanding, she is sure to blossom into a wonderful companion.Ursula has arrived with a bilateral Grade 2 patella luxation that may improve with gentle exercise but will need to be monitored in the home. Her adopters will need to be aware of this as it may not be covered by insurance. She has also arrived with an umbilical hernia that has been repaired during her spay.

name: Jinx
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need a secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have a sore eye that is being monitored.

Jinx is an exceptionally frightened boy who has come into our care from a breeder. He will do all he can to run away and hide from us, and it is heartbreaking to witness just how scared he is. However, after just over a month in our care, his personality is slowly beginning to shine through. Although he remains very wary and unsure, he is starting to make lovely little steps forward. He now gets excited when he sees a familiar face, happily wagging his tail and sniffing a hand, even if he isn't quite ready for anyone to come too close. These may seem like small steps, but for Jinx they are huge achievements, and it is wonderful to see his confidence growing.

Jinx has also begun harness training and is taking to it really well! He is now venturing down to our big play yard, where his playful puppy side is starting to emerge. It is lovely to see him becoming a little more curious about the world around him as he gradually learns that he is safe.

Jinx will need a kind and confident resident dog in his new home, as this will be a much-needed support system to help him settle and gain confidence. We have not yet cat tested him, but given what we have seen so far, we feel it is unlikely that he would be suitable to share a home with cats.

As Jinx has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. His harness training is progressing well, but his adopters will need to continue this gently and at his own pace. He will need a quiet, experienced home with people who understand ex-breeding dogs and appreciate that building trust with him will take considerable time, patience and kindness.

Due to his nervous nature, Jinx is currently a flight risk and will need a very secure garden with boundaries of at least 6ft. He may also need to be muzzled for formal handling, such as veterinary visits, to help keep everyone safe and make these experiences as comfortable as possible for him.

Jinx arrived with a sore eye, so we are continuing to clean it and make sure he is comfortable while we assess this further.

Jinx still has a long way to go, but he is making progress every day, and it is lovely to see his gentle, playful personality beginning to emerge. He needs a very special home filled with patience and love, where his adopters understand that trust will take time and are happy to celebrate every little achievement along the way. With the support of a kind canine companion and people who will let him move at his own pace, we hope Jinx will continue to blossom and discover the safe and loving life he deserves.

Jinx has been given the Gift of Life by Lesley Beattie

Jinx has now been with us just over a month, and although Jinx is still a very scared boy, his personality is slowly starting to shine through. Jinx has now begun harness training and is taking to it really well! He even now adventures down to our big play yard where his puppy side is really starting to show!  Jinx also now gets really excited to see me, he doesn’t allow me very close but he will happily wag his tail, and sniff my hand!

This might sound like the smallest thing, but for myself and Jinx this is a massive win! Every day is confidence is showing more and more.

Jinx just needs a home with loads of patience and love, and people who will understand trust is going to a long time.I can’t wait to see Jinx blossom more and more each day.

Jinx is an exceptionally frightened boy who has come into our care from a breeder.He will do all he can to run away and hide from us, and it is heartbreaking to witness just how scared he is. Despite his trust issues, he has allowed a small amount of fuss, although he remains very wary and unsure of our intentions. He will need lots of time, patience and gentle handling while he learns that he is safe.Because of this, Jinx will need another kind and confident dog in his new home, and this dog will be a much-needed support system for him as he begins to settle and gain some confidence.We have not yet cat tested Jinx, but given what we have seen from him so far, it is unlikely that he would be suitable to share a home with cats.As Jinx has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. He will need a quiet, experienced home with adopters who understand ex-breeding dogs and are prepared to be very patient with him.Due to his nervous nature, Jinx is currently a flight risk and will need a very secure garden with boundaries of at least 6ft. He is a very scared boy and may need to be muzzled for formal handling eg. vet visits.Jinx has arrived with a sore eye, so we are keeping on top of cleaning it and making sure he is comfortable while we assess this further.Jinx has a long way to go, but the fact that he has already allowed a little fuss shows that there is a gentle side beneath all those worries. We hope that with the right canine companion, experienced adopters and lots of patience, he will slowly learn to trust and discover the safe and loving life he deserves.

name: Paris
description:
I'd like a quiet, experienced, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

30-09-26 Paris is a scared girly who is not used to being handled. She has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start and is not a fan of human touch at the moment.

When we have needed to get close to Paris for health checks, we have had to carefully corner her so that we can pick her up. She panics and shakes, but she does allow us to handle her and, once she is safely in our arms, she eventually cuddles into us and allows us to carry out her checks. This shows us that although she is very frightened, she is beginning to understand that we are not going to hurt her.

Paris will need another kind and confident dog in her new home, and this dog will be a much-needed support system for her as she settles in and starts to find her confidence.

As Paris has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. She will need an ex-breeding experienced, adult-only home with adopters who understand just how much patience and reassurance she will need.

Paris is a very worried little girl right now, but once she is given the security of being held, we can see that there is a much softer side to her. We hope that with time, patience and the support of a reassuring canine companion, she will slowly learn to trust and enjoy the happy new start she deserves.

Paris has been given the Gift of Life by Margaret Hunter

name: Irene
description:
I can live with older, dog savvy teenagers, aged 16+ who respect my space.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I am new to lead walking, and would like to continue this once I have settled in.

I have lived in a home before so know the basics.

I have Grade 3 bilateral luxating patellas.

21-10-26 Irene is a nervous little lady who has come to us from a breeder. Although she is still unsure, she shows lovely glimpses of wanting to be confident. If you are patient with her and crouch down to her level, she'll quietly come over to give you little kisses, showing just how much love she has to give once she feels safe.

Irene will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home that she can lean on as she learns about trust and settles into home life. She has recently moved to a foster home where she is learning all about the routines of home life. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who are sensible and will allow her time to settle in. She will need a home that has experience with ex-breeders that can provide her with the assurance she deserves.

Irene is new to lead walking but has enjoyed plenty of walks with her foster mummy and is gaining her confidence on the lead. She will need a home without cats as she has met cats while out and about and was a little too interested in them. Irene is a truly lovely girl who just needs time, patience and plenty of TLC. With an understanding home and a canine friend by her side, we're sure she will continue to grow in confidence and become a wonderful companion.

Irene has been assessed by our vets who have noted that she has Grade 3 bilateral luxating patellas. These aren't causing her any issues at the moment and may improve with gentle exercise as she builds muscle. They will need to be monitored by her adopters and their vet and her adopters should be aware that any future treatment relating to her luxating patellas will not be covered by insurance.

Irene has been given the Gift of Life by Trudie Williams
