name: Gigi
description:
I will need an adult-only home that understands me.

I need a resident dog Cocker Spaniel size or larger to be my friend.

I would like a secure garden with 6ft+ fences.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

Gigi is a very worried lady who has come to us from a breeder. When she first arrived, she was terrified of people and would try to escape any area she was in if she thought someone might approach her. Thankfully, she has made lovely progress and is now much more relaxed around the carers she knows. She has settled into her routine and will even come over for little sniffs when her kennel friends approach for attention. She is also much easier to handle now and, when worried, will retreat to her safe corner rather than trying to flee.

Despite her progress, Gigi remains a flight risk and her safety must always be a priority. Her adopters will need to be very safety-conscious and have a very secure garden with fencing at least 6ft high. Moving to a new environment may cause her confidence to regress, so precautions will be essential to keep her safe. We hope to begin harness training with her, but this will need to be introduced slowly and carefully. Double-leading will be absolutely essential for a long time to come.

Gigi absolutely loves other dogs and is delighted to meet them, wanting to be friends with everyone! She will need a kind, confident resident dog who genuinely enjoys canine company and can take her under their wing, helping her feel secure and guiding her through the different aspects of home life. She will need this dog to be Cocker Spaniel sized or larger and cannot be homed with smaller dogs.

As Gigi has never lived in a home before, she will need patient adopters who can help her learn about house training, lead walking and all the new experiences that come with being a much-loved pet. She needs an adult-only home with experience of ex-breeding dogs, where her fears are understood and she is given the time, space and reassurance she needs to settle at her own pace.

Gigi has come a long way already, and with the right home, a loving canine companion and plenty of time and patience, we believe she has the potential to continue blossoming. Her new family must be prepared to put in as much time and effort as she needs, taking everything slowly and steadily so she can learn that life can be a wonderful place to be.

Gigi has been given the Gift of Life by Rachel Morris

When Gigi was first moved in to her current section she was terrified, she would try to jump out of any area she was in if she felt a human may be getting near to her, now she has settled into the routine and knows the carers of the section well, she is far more relaxed with them, even coming up for little sniffs when her kennel friends do. She is much easier to handle now too and will freeze in her safe corner in her kennel rather than trying to flee.

Despite the progress she has made her new adopters will be very safety conscious with a very secure garden to ensure that if she were to regress when brought in to a new environment she would always still be safe. We feel that with the progress she has made we can now start to harness train her, this will be a slow process always keeping her safety at the forefront of our minds and double leading her will be absolutely essential for a long time to come.

Gigi loves other dogs, any dog she meets makes her very happy and she truly wants to be a friend to them all, so she will need a resident dog who actively loves having a companion and will really take her under their wing and help to guide her through all aspects of home life.

In the right home she will thrive but her new humans will need to be prepared to put in as much time, effort and patience as she needs and to take it slow and steady so she truly learns to see that life is actually pretty good after all.

Gigi is a very worried lady who has come to us from a breeder and is understandably very nervous and uncomfortable around people. She can be considered a flight risk as she will do her best to get away when she feels worried, so she will need very slow and gentle introductions to the world around her.

Gigi is going to need lots of TLC, patience and understanding from her new family as she learns that she is safe and begins to build her confidence. She will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to and lean on for reassurance as she settles in.

Gigi has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she learns about house training and walking on a lead. These things may take some time, and she will need a family who is happy to let her progress at her own pace. She will need a very secure garden with fences 6ft+.

Gigi will need an adult-only home with ex-breeding experience, where her needs can be understood and she can receive the patience and reassurance she deserves. With time, love and the support of a confident canine companion, we hope Gigi will slowly learn to trust and become the happy, active girl we know she can be.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Murphy
description:
Meet MURPHY, a gentle, loving, and resilient small boy around 4.5 years old, who resembles a charming mix of Corgi and Chihuahua. He is a Ukraine war dog in need of a safe haven.

Available for a foster-to-adopt. Already in UK: Clapham (London), SW11. Adoption fee reduced.

He lost one eye in a horrific incident in Ukraine, but his spirit remains unbroken. He’s now in the UK and looking for a forever home where he can be cherished. Sadly, the family who took him in feels they are not the right match for him and are unable to meet his needs.

They have provided a thorough evaluation of MURPHY, which you can read below.

Rescue Story:MURPHY’s story is one of love, resilience, and heartbreak. He was abandoned in a communal garden in Ukraine, where he was embraced by the local residents. They cared for him, and he became part of their extended family, playing with children and happily resting in his little kennel.

Tragically, some cruel teenagers thought it would be amusing to chase MURPHY and throw a petard into his kennel. After the explosion, MURPHY was left severely injured, his face burned and bleeding, and his eye tragically lost. However, despite this horror, MURPHY’s spirit remained unbroken.

He was rushed to a clinic, treated, and later brought into a rescue. Through it all, MURPHY continued to trust humans, showing the true resilience of a dog’s heart.

A Word from His Current Family:“ He is a lovely little dog, with a strong and great spirit. Murphy is a rescue from Ukraine who came to us in June 2024. He only has one eye due to an incident where he was attacked by some teenagers who threw a firework / explosive into his little den.

Since then he was taken into care and fostered for.

A highly independent little soul, he loves his alone time and is never anxious in these periods. He loves his sleep and will find sun spots and cozy little nooks to snuggle up in.

Positives? Good to be left alone for short periods, very calm and sleeps a lot? Doesn’t destroy things in house? Independent? Enjoys good play time and belly rubs when he rolls over? Not a fussy eater? Will sit for snacks and treats? Handsome? Very low maintenance, will shed a couple times a year.? Travels well, loves car and train journeys

Needs? Child free house? A quieter house, less footfall to not disturb him? Only dog in house

Things to know? Give him space and wait for him to come to you. He will and he loves chin and ear scratches? Resource guard, work on splitting his meals up and make him back away from food bowl before topping up. He has improved.? Don’t pick him up? Leave alone when in his bed (trained safe space)? Keep on lead when on walks? Takes pain relief pills for previous accident.– has snapped on occasion, when was misunderstood, but not regularly and not his fault. Needs patience and understanding for all he’s been through

Due to his injuries and impaired vision he can be easily startled if approached from his right.

Requiring a very calm and peaceful life. Super low maintenance and highly independent, he is equally happy when alone or in company of owners. Give him space and wait for him to come to you, he loves chin and ear scratches. He’s a great little dog to have around and keep you company.

He will nuzzle up to you for some love and scratches and then spend the rest of night tucked up in his bed. He has adapted well to his new life in the UK and is very healthy.

Fully vaccinated and blood tests all came back healthy. He doesn’t require long walks and can be tired out after half hour to an hour”

MURPHY is fully healthy (but missing one eye), neutered. All core vaccines are complete, microchipped, and C.Brucella tested (owners will receive a licensed laboratory test certificate).

name: Iris
description:
Iris is a 2-3 year old female Lurcher. She is great with people. Iris will need a pet and child-free home.

We are looking for either a foster or a forever home. She’s a fun-loving dog. Who just wants to be loved? If you think you can offer her lots of love and a sofa to sleep on.

name: Millie
description:
Millie is a beautiful temperament, always happy, loving cross-breed girl of around 2 years old.

She is super friendly with everyone – kids, dogs, cats. Great on the lead. Housetrained. Based in Peterborough, available for foster-to-adopt. Reduced adoption fees

Unfortunately, a few days ago, Millie had to go to boarding kennels as all our current fosters are fully booked. While this is likely one of the best kennels you can find, staffed by true dog lovers with great facilities, an on-site behaviorist, and a focus on rehabilitation, it’s still not the same as a home.

They offer wonderful care, take the dogs on walks, and play with them, but it can’t replace the love and comfort of a real family. We’re praying that this sweet girl finds her forever home soon.

Before this Millie was at foster in UK and this is what they say:

“Millie is a very sweet, attractive and affectionate young dog. She likes people and to be with people and is normally docile and friendly. She likes to be stroked and groomed and to have her belly rubbed.

She likes exploring but doesn’t try and escape from the garden or run off when out for a walk. She likes to play with toys, especially in the evening out in the garden. She will readily sit on command and shake a paw!

She is very good off the lead, walking along paths, in fields and in the woods etc in the countryside, and she will regularly look back and check that you are there and come back when called.

She is very friendly with people she meets and will regularly sniff them (to check they are human) as you walk along, though she is slightly nervous of other larger dogs until she gets to know them. She will happily chase and play with other dogs she feels comfortable with. If they are too much she will do a little growl and they will usually back off.

However, we have come across a few behavioural issues. The main issue appears ‘resource guarding’ and the things she guards have increased and changed whilst she has been with us. This can be unpredictable and takes us by surprise at times. For instance we might be happily working in the same room as Millie who’s in her bed, coming and going and talking to her.

Suddenly she will change and growl, snarl if we re-enter the room. She also will suddenly and unpredictably snarl in other places where she’s lying down. Another example is that we are both hesitant of trying to move her off the sofa.

The only safe way is to call her from another room, sometimes with a treat to lure her. This may be because for some reason Millie has not really settled with us after nearly four weeks and still feels insecure.

I think Millie will need to be with family who are experienced with dogs, who can interpret her body language and behaviour, and be able train with her to reduce and prevent her very marked resource guarding (rescue will be happy to provide useful and working materials to treat it). I think this shouldn’t be a family with young children but teenagers and older children should be okay if they are aware of what not to do.”

MILLIE is active but not hyper, always happy, not pushy. Very loving and loves cuddles and fuss. Loves people company and being nearby.

MILLIE is very smart, loves learning new things. But the most she likes is walks being active and having attention from people.MILLIE is good in the car and loves it.

MILLIE has no known health issues. Spayed, vaccinated, microchipped. Brucella C. tested.

name: Ava
description:
Ava is a 6-year-old female Cross-Breed who is very friendly and playful.

She has been neutered, microchipped, and vaccinated, making her fully prepared for her new home.

Ava weighs approximately 28 kg and stands around 48 cm tall.

This sweet girl is eager to find a home where she can be loved and cared for.

Ava’s playful nature and friendly disposition make her a delightful companion.

She would thrive in a home where she can receive plenty of attention and affection.

name: Bailey
description:
He is a super boy and a lovely goofball. Bailey is neutered, vaccinated, and microchipped, making him ready for his forever home.

Standing at approximately 60cm tall and weighing around 40 kg, he is a friendly and sizeable companion.

Despite his large stature, Bailey’s gentle nature makes him an ideal addition to any loving household.

He is eager to find a home where he can share his affection and playful energy.

Bailey’s charming personality makes him a delightful companion for anyone seeking a loyal canine friend.

name: Pennie
description:
Pennie is an 13 months old, female, cross-breed pup who, along with her siblings, faced abandonment in woodland in Romania at a very young age.

Fortunately, they found refuge in a foster shelter where they have been nurtured ever since.

This sweet and slightly shy pup exhibits a calm demeanor, making her an ideal companion for those with experience in dog ownership.

As a good-sized medium dog, Pennie will undergo neutering before embarking on her journey to a new home in the UK.

Her health is meticulously documented in her pet passport, with full vaccination and microchipping completed.

Comprehensive blood tests have been conducted to ensure a smooth integration into her new life.

Pennie, being fully cat-tested with a video available for potential adopters, proves her compatibility with feline friends.

Ideally suited for a family with older children due to her size, Pennie would thrive in an environment where her adopters possess previous dog ownership experience.

To facilitate a seamless transition, we offer full rescue backup and a commitment to ongoing support, ensuring the continued well-being of our canine charges.

Pennie eagerly awaits a loving home, ready to bring joy and companionship to a family in the UK.

name: Holly
description:
Holly, 1 year old female Cross-Breed, and her two sisters were found dumped by waste bins in an alley in Romania at six weeks old.

They have been in a foster shelter since then, and their English foster mum has brought them on well.

They are in a pen with some other pups and a surrogate mum and dad dog, which teaches them doggy manners!

Holly is neutered and fully vaccinated. She is also microchipped.

She would be delivered directly to her new owners once admin checks have been done.

It would be wonderful if she could have a doggy friend to live with, but this is not essential.

Two of her kennel mates have already travelled to their new homes in the UK, and it would be lovely if Holly could too.

Full rescue backup is given on all of our dogs.

name: Freya
description:
Freya, a 5 year old female Labrador Cross, has been patiently waiting in the foster shelter for quite a while after being rescued from a kill shelter in Romania.

We can’t understand why someone hasn’t fallen for her before.

Freya loves attention from her humans and lives with other dogs.

She has been neutered and fully vaccinated as well as microchipped.

She would be delivered directly to her new adopter once admin checks have been carried out.

Please consider this lovely girl for a place on the Happy Bus to a new life here in the UK.

name: Inky
description:
Inky, also known as Blinky, is a very cute whippety lurcher boy of around 2 years old, looking for a special forever home.

He is a loving, affectionate boy who thrives on companionship and enjoys being part of the family. When he arrived in foster care, almost 8 months ago, he was in a very poor physical condition due to previous neglect.

He had flat feet caused by a lack of proper nutrition and calcium, as well as severe corns on his feet and infected toes which made walking very painful for him.

The corns later required surgery. He underwent three weeks of daily bandage changes and treatment, which he handled incredibly well.

His feet have improved significantly, but adopters should be aware that corns can recur in some dogs and may require monitoring and future veterinary care.

EGLR are happy to contribute towards this. Inky is great on the lead and enjoys his walks, he can become very boisterous and can be a little reactive at first when seeing other dogs and very jumpy when meeting new people but this is just excitement.

His recall is very good in a secure environment. His absolute favourite game is fetch, and he can happily spend time chasing and retrieving his toys.

He also loves trips to a secure field where he can stretch his legs and enjoy himself. Around the home, Inky is a real cuddle bug.

He loves nothing more than snuggling up on the sofa with his people and will happily curl up beside you for an evening of relaxation.

He sleeps well through the night, although if given the opportunity, he may quietly sneak onto the bed and burrow under the duvet, especially when it’s cold! very whippety behaviour. He is fully house trained and not destructive.

Inky travels brilliantly in the car and settles quickly, making him an excellent companion for adventures. He can be left for up to four hours with another dog.

He may bark initially when left but soon settles down. He generally gets on well with other dogs, although he can be a little dominant around some male dogs.

Because of this, he would be best suited to living with a female dog. Due to some issues around female handlers, Inky is looking for an adult-only home with male owners.

He won’t cope living with children and needs a home where there are no visiting children. Inky has worked with professional trainers and has made great progress.

His foster carers have learned techniques that help him succeed, and support can continue for adopters based in the Worcestershire and Gloucestershire areas. Inky is a wonderful, loyal dog with so much love to give.

In the right environment, with understanding, dog experienced owners who can continue the guidance he’s already received, he will make a devoted and affectionate companion.

This dear boy has been through so much in his short life and experienced so much pain, inky really deserves the best home we can get him.

name: Liquorice
description:
Liquorice, 15 month old male Lurcher, is quite honestly one of the sweetest, silliest and most lovable boys you could ever wish to meet. He is an incredibly sociable lad who absolutely adores people.

I genuinely haven’t met a person he doesn’t greet like a long-lost friend!

Even when he was having to attend the vets twice a day to have his wound cleaned, he would arrive with his happy, waggy tail, seemingly forgetting all about the discomfort of his visits and simply looking for love, attention and cuddles.

One of the lovely things about him is how adaptable he is.

He has enjoyed lots of house visits, happily meeting and greeting new people, and has even had a couple of overnight stays at different foster homes, settling in straight away as though he’d lived there forever.

He’s also had the opportunity to meet lots of different dogs during these visits, and making new friends is definitely one of his favourite things to do!

Liquorice is continuing to build up his confidence with being left alone and is now managing a couple of hours after having been walked and fed.

This is something his new family will need to continue working on gradually. He’s an excellent traveller in the car and really is a pleasure to take out and about.

On walks, Liquorice can be a little strong on the lead. Some of this is down to him adapting to his new walking gait as a three-legged boy, and some is simply his excitement at being out exploring the world!

He’s getting fitter and stronger every day and is already enjoying around 30 minutes in the morning and 40 minutes in the evening.

At weekends, we sometimes swap this for one longer walk. He’s still a young boy with plenty of energy, and as his fitness continues to improve, he’ll need a family happy to provide him with the exercise and adventures he enjoys.

And finally, we must mention Liquorice’s other great passion in life… TOYS! Liquorice is a master toy destroyer. If there’s stuffing inside, he will find it!

His new home will need to provide him with a plentiful supply of toys for him to lovingly de-stuff, as this is quite possibly his favourite pastime. So, what sort of home is Liquorice looking for?

We think this lovely boy would be happiest in a home: Without cats. With another friendly dog to play with and share adventures.

With children aged 12 and over. With a secure garden where he can enjoy some playtime and burn off some of that cheeky energy.

Liquorice has been through so much, yet he continues to greet every day and everyone he meets with the happiest of hearts. He doesn’t let having three legs stop him enjoying life, and he has so much love to give.

We’re looking for a family who will embrace his cheeky personality, enjoy his enthusiasm for life, continue supporting his progress and, most importantly, love him unconditionally.

Could you be the one to give this very special boy the forever home he’s been waiting for? We think you’re going to fall head over heels for him.

name: Jam
description:
Jam is a female mixed breed puppy aged around 5 months. As a guess she will be medium sized when fully grown. Jam fostered in Norwich, Norfolk.

Jam has grown up at the public shelter in Botosani. We met her on our most recent visit and she is one of the lucky pups to come on transport to England.

Due to being a young puppy, we are looking for a forever family where there is an adult at home for most of the day. All puppy adopters will need to work on training throughout their young life and anticipate accidents.

Isn’t yet cat tested but young enough to be trained to be appropriate around a cat.

name: Walter
description:
Our extra special boy Walter is approximately eight years old and a rather large hound of sorts. Walter weighs twenty-seven kilos and measures fourteen inches from shoulder to paw.

Very sadly Walter has spent half of his life in our Cyprus shelter having been surrendered by his owner.

Walter is the absolute favourite of the shelter staff and volunteers. His attractiveness is instigated by his wisdom, prudence and calm demeanour.

Walter has a near mystic charm which wins hearts and minds rapidly. Such a stunning boy with a huge presence.

Absolutely a handsome chap with a wonderful coat and ears that are totally extraordinary. Really Walter could hardly be more deserving and will make a fabulous new family member for a very fortunate adopting family.

Walter exudes charm and elegance on his lead and enjoys his time in the car. He seems to mix perfectly well with other dogs, cats and children.

name: Jello
description:
Jello is a female mixed breed puppy aged around 5 months. As a guess she will be medium sized when fully grown. Jello fostered in Norwich, Norfolk.

Jello has grown up at the public shelter in Botosani. We met her on our most recent visit and she is one of the lucky pups to come on transport to England.

Due to being a young puppy, we are looking for a forever family where there is an adult at home for most of the day. All puppy adopters will need to work on training throughout their young life and anticipate accidents.

Isn’t yet cat tested but young enough to be trained to be appropriate around a cat.

name: Reyna
description:
Reyna is an eight year old female Border Collie. Reyna is in a wonderful foster home in Cambridgeshire.

She shares her foster home with several resident dogs and although we think she’s lived a sheltered life without much interaction, with their guidance, she’s really learned how to interact and enjoy the company of other dogs.

Although very nervous when she first arrived, she has slowly but surely come out of her shell with the guidance of her foster family and has even been for some little adventures to a cafe!

She can still be shy of new people but she’s affectionate with everyone, especially her foster mum who’s a firm favourite since she does all the walks!

Her character is coming out as she gains confidence and she can be a lovable cheeky monkey! She’s a real joy to watch as she grows and learns that the world can be a fun and safe place to be.

She travels well in the car, eager to jump in for a walk! She’s also picked up house training very well too. Her foster mum calls her the perfect dog.

She gets on well with all the resident dogs but the other resident collie is a firm favourite! She is looking for a home with a kind and patient family who can carry on all the amazing work of her foster home

Reyna is a Border Collie. Her Spanish passport says she is eight years old but the vet thinks she might be younger.

Reyna was given to the shelter in Spain along with her three puppies (Ares, Sena and Zeus) by a family who kept her outside her whole life. We think she had been chained up for most of that time and hadn’t had the chance to interact with humans much or other dogs.

Reyna’s Spanish passport says she’s almost 8 years old but the vet thinks she might be younger.

If you are interested in giving wonderful Reyna a home, she is available at Setter Brittany Pointer Rescue. Reyna is currently in Cambridgeshire but she is ready to travel to her forever home. Will that be with you?

name: Mandy
description:
Mandy is a 5-year-old female Cross-Breed. She’s a calm, gentle soul who has already been spayed and fully vaccinated, weighing around 23 kilograms.

Mandy is currently safe in a private shelter in Romania after being rescued from a kill shelter earlier this year — and now she’s patiently waiting for her forever home.

This lovely girl has a relaxed, easy-going personality. She loves simple pleasures like pottering around a garden and finding a comfy spot to nap in.

Mandy doesn’t need a high-energy household; she’s happiest in a calm environment where she can enjoy her surroundings and be close to her people.

She gets along beautifully with other dogs and has no trouble sharing her space with feline friends either. Mandy’s sociable yet serene nature makes her a wonderful companion for homes with other pets.

She could also live with dog-savvy children aged 10 and above, as long as they understand her gentle and steady temperament.

Although Mandy enjoys the company of other dogs, she doesn’t necessarily need one in her home. She’s quite content being the only dog as long as she receives love, care, and companionship from her humans. What she does need, however, is a secure garden — a place to wander, relax, and soak up the sunshine.

Mandy represents everything lovely about a rescue dog: calm, affectionate, and grateful for every bit of kindness shown to her.

Her adopters will also receive full rescue backup and support throughout the adoption process and for the lifetime of the dog, ensuring Mandy’s smooth transition into her new life.

Home checks and an adoption donation apply, as the rescue ensures every placement is the perfect fit. Whoever opens their home to Mandy will be rewarded with a loyal, gentle friend who embodies peace and love in every wag of her tail.

name: Duke
description:
Duke is a six year old male Pointer. Duke is a very handsome boy!

Duke was handed in to the shelter we work with in North Spain by a hunter as he was no longer wanted. He has a slender and elegant figure, he is of medium size and a balanced character and is respectful of the other dogs at the kennels.

Duke currently shares his kennel with a female Setter. He shares the space without problems including at dinner time.

Duke is a little shy if he doesn’t know you, but he quickly gains confidence and approaches timidly seeking cuddles and caresses.

His recall is good within the confines of the shelter but it would be a different matter on an exciting walk. He loves to run around the enclosure and stretch his long legs.

If you are interested in giving wonderful Duke a home, he is available at Setter Brittany Pointer Rescue. Duke is currently in Spain but he is ready to travel to his forever home in the UK.

name: Kylo
description:
Kylo is a 4 year old, medium sized, lab-cross and is literally the friendliest boy. He simply adores being around humans and will be the best companion.

Oh and he knows some tricks! When he arrived at the shelter he was microchipped so he had some sort of home at some point in his life.

He craves love and attention from everyone he meets, even if just meeting for the first time. He’s very smart and will be a joy to train.

Kylo is a very sweet boy and has a puppy-like energy where he is just happy and excited to be with you and show off his tricks. And he’s very food oriented!

Some dogs in the shelter he accepts, others he doesn’t. Although this can be a product of the stress of shelter life, it’s best if he is an only dog.

Kylo can be quite energetic and will likely need an active home. He would even make a good running buddy. He already walks well on the leash.

Kylo can be adopted in the UK or Cyprus. His adoption fees are sponsored so, if travelling to the UK, we are just asking for travel costs to be covered.

He is ready to fly. He is vaccinated, castrated, and has had a full health check and blood tests for infectious diseases.

Full rescue back-up is provided by Saving Souls Animal Rescue, a UK-based registered charity.

Foster placement, foster view to adopt, and adoption all considered.

name: Captain
description:
Captain is a 5 year old male Cross-Breed.

Captain came into our care from another rescue and since being with us has ensured every day is full of fun and excitement.

He is obsessed with food and isn’t guilty of stealing your lunch.

Very bouncy and full of joy Captain will require a home with older teenagers due to his long legs and is happy as the only animal.

Sadly, he is avoidant of other dogs and prefers human companionship.

His prey drive is very high, and he is potentially Bull lurcher in breed, so he is walked on lead with a muzzle and enjoys off lead exercise within a secure field.

name: Daisy
description:
DAISY — SHE NEEDS A HOME TO SHOW WHO SHE REALLY IS!

Daisy is a three year old cross breed female.

Daisy is always smiling. Even in kennels, even while keeping herself just a little apart, that beautiful smile is there. She is three years old, small, gentle and full of the sweetest little character.

She loves other dogs, enjoys being around people and carries a quiet happiness that never seems to leave her face. But we do not believe kennels show us the whole Daisy. She is not scared. She is not timid.

She simply keeps a little distance around people, as though she is waiting for life to become softer before she gives us everything that is inside her. And we truly believe that life will begin in a home. Away from kennel noise.

Away from constant movement. Inside a peaceful space where she can learn the rhythm of her people, find her favourite bed and finally understand that she belongs there.

That is where Daisy will bloom. We can already see glimpses of the girl waiting underneath.

A loving little soul. A smiling companion. An adorable character who wants to be close, but needs the right surroundings to fully relax and shine. Daisy is wonderful with other dogs, and a calm, friendly dog may help her settle beautifully into family life.

She is never pushy or demanding. She simply needs a home where closeness can grow naturally.

Kennels are keeping Daisy waiting between two lives. She has left the kill shelter behind, but she has not yet reached the life she was saved for. She should be waking up in a warm home.

She should be walking beside her people. She should be carrying that lovely smile from room to room, slowly becoming more affectionate, more confident and more herself with every passing day.

Daisy does not need fixing. She needs the chance to live. And we believe that once she steps out of kennels and into the right home, this beautiful little girl will finally show everyone just how much love, happiness and personality she has been carrying all along.

DAISY — AT A GLANCE:3 years oldSmall mixed-breed girlWonderful with other dogsLoving, gentle and always smilingAdorable, never pushy and full of quiet characterNeeds a calm home where she can relax and truly bloomCould happily live with a friendly canine companion

Fully vaccinatedSpayed4D testedBrucellosis testedMicrochippedFull RBU

Please message our adoption page if you can give Daisy the home life she needs to become everything we know she can be. Daisy is already smiling. Now she needs a home that will give her every reason to shine!

name: Ted
description:
Meet Ted – A Little Frenchie Who’s Finally Ready to Be Loved

He came into our care as a UK rescue after being pulled from a local pound by one of our trusted pound pullers.

Before that, Ted had been seized by the Metropolitan Police as part of a cruelty case, and when he arrived with us, it was clear he’d endured a great deal of neglect. His little body was covered in fleas and he was suffering from a severe flea allergy.

His skin was red, sore and painfully itchy, and he’d lost much of the fur across his back and around his face. It must have been incredibly uncomfortable, but despite everything he’d been through, Ted’s gentle nature still shone through.

Fast forward to today, and this handsome little man is a completely different dog.

Ted has now been fully assessed by our vet, has been castrated, is responding brilliantly to treatment, and his beautiful coat is growing back nicely. Best of all, his happy, affectionate personality is beginning to shine brighter every day.

What Ted is Like • Exceptionally affectionate and loving

Loves nothing more than cuddles and human company

Loves being close to his favourite person Ted has formed an incredibly strong bond with our General Manager and absolutely adores her.

He thrives on companionship and is happiest when he’s close to the person he loves. He can sometimes bark when meeting strangers, but this isn’t aggression—it’s simply his way of letting everyone know they’re there.

Once he realises everything is okay, his lovely personality quickly takes over.

Ted’s Ideal Home Although Ted gets along well with other dogs, we feel he’d truly flourish as an only dog where he doesn’t have to share his favourite person’s attention.

His perfect home would ideally be with a single person, preferably a lady, who is looking for a devoted little companion.

Someone who is home for much of the day would suit Ted perfectly, as he simply loves being part of everyday life and doesn’t ask for much more than a comfy bed, gentle walks and plenty of cuddles.

A calm home where he can continue to feel safe, secure and cherished would be everything this little boy has ever dreamed of.

Why We Love Ted Ted is proof that kindness can change a life.

Despite the neglect he suffered, he hasn’t lost his trust in people.

Instead, he greets each day with a wagging tail, a hopeful heart and an endless supply of love to give.

He isn’t looking for a life of excitement or adventure. He’s looking for his person. Someone who will adore him just as much as he’ll adore them.

After everything this little boy has endured, we so desperately want to find him the forever home he has always deserved. Could that be with you?

Could You Give Ted His Happy Ending? If you think you could offer Ted the safe, loving home he’s been waiting for, please visit: www.savingandrehomingstrays.org

Potential adopters must be willing to travel to Ayr to meet and collect Ted. Let’s make sure the rest of Ted’s story is filled with nothing but love, comfort and happiness.

name: Willow
description:
WILLOW — A LITTLE DOG WITH EVERYTHING YOU COULD EVER WISH FOR!

Willow is a two-year-old female cross breed.

Some dogs are easy to love from the very first moment.

At only two years old, this beautiful middle-to-smaller girl has the kind of character people spend years hoping to find.

She is loving.Kind.Gentle.Clever.Eager to please.

But more than anything, Willow is simply a joy to be around.

She gets along beautifully with other dogs, loves people and is wonderful with children. She has such an easy, lovely way about her — friendly without being overwhelming, affectionate without demanding, happy just to be included and close to those she loves.

Willow is smart and willing to learn. She listens, she connects and she wants to make you happy.

She is the kind of little dog who would bring warmth into a home without ever asking for much in return.

A walk beside you.A soft place to sleep.A family to call her own.

And Willow would give back everything she has — her trust, her loyalty, her happiness and her whole gentle heart.

Willow does not need to become the perfect family dog.

She is simply waiting for the family who will finally see that she belongs with them.

WILLOW — AT A GLANCE:2 years oldMiddle-to-smaller-sized girlLoving, kind, gentle and affectionateSmart and eager to pleaseWonderful with other dogsGreat with childrenLoves people and family lifeA joyful, easy and truly special little dog

WILLOW IS IN PERFECT HEALTH:Fully vaccinatedSpayed4D testedBrucellosis tested

Please message us if you believe Willow could be the little girl your home has been waiting for.

name: Donald
description:
DONALD — EVERYTHING A FAMILY DOG SHOULD BE!

Donald is a three year old male cross breed.

Donald is the dog people describe when they tell us what they are dreaming of. A gentle dog. A calm dog. A dog who loves people, understands other animals and can be trusted around children.

A dog who walks into a room and brings peace with him. Donald is all of that. He is three years old, middle-sized, and has the most beautiful nature we could ever wish for in a dog.

He adores people. He is wonderfully gentle with children, fantastic with other dogs and friendly with cats.

But those words still do not explain what it feels like to be around him.

Being with Donald feels like being close to something completely good. He looks at you with that radiant smile, comes near with such softness and settles beside you as though being together is the most natural thing in the world.

Loving Donald happens before you even realise it. We can see him beside a child, quietly watching over them. We can see him sharing his home with another dog and becoming their closest friend. We can see him carefully greeting the family cat.

We can see his smiling face waiting at the door, his head resting in someone’s lap and his beautiful presence becoming part of every ordinary day. And that is what breaks our hearts.

Because Donald should already have this life. He should already have someone who knows the sound of his paws walking through their home.

Someone who kisses his head before bed. Someone who looks at that beautiful smile every morning and knows they chose one of the finest dogs they could ever have found.

Donald is one of our rescue’s favourite dogs. We know him. We know the goodness he carries. We know how easy he is to be around and how deeply he deserves to be loved.

He asks for so little from the world, yet he brings kindness into every place he enters. All we want now is for Donald to find a home where that kindness will finally come back to him.

A home that will love him with the same gentleness he gives to everyone else. A family who will understand that they have not adopted just a wonderful dog. They have been given a gift.

3 years oldMiddle-sized boyCalm, loving, gentle and deeply kindWonderful and gentle with childrenFantastic with other dogsCat-friendlyAdores peopleRadiant, smiling and beautifully easy to share life withOne of our rescue’s most loved dogs

DONALD’S HEALTH:Fully vaccinatedNeutered4D testedBrucellosis testedMicrochippedFull RBU

Please message us if Donald feels like the calm, loving boy your home has been waiting for! He really is a one-of-a-kind boy!

name: Rose
description:
The sweetest Rose, nearly 4 years old, neutered, medium-sized, German short haired pointer.

Sweet Rose has been in our Cyprus shelter since September 2025, quietly waiting for someone to see her.

She’s the kind of dog people walk past without realising how much she’s hurting — gentle, sensitive, and trying her best to cope in a place that overwhelms her.

Rose can be frightened at times, and the truth is, shelter life will never help her grow in the way she needs. The noise, the chaos, the constant movement… it’s simply too much for a soft soul like hers.

What she needs is a calm, patient home where she can finally exhale and learn that the world isn’t scary.

She isn’t a difficult dog — she’s a worried one. And worried dogs blossom beautifully when given love, kindness, and time. And, knowing what pointers are like, she is desperate to show some affection to humans that she can trust.

Rose would thrive in a quiet home with people who understand that progress comes in gentle steps. Someone who will celebrate the small wins, offer reassurance when she’s unsure, and show her what safety feels like.

Once she trusts you, her sweetness shines through. She is frightened of children so she can only be homed with a family if children are over the age of 15 yrs old.

This girl has waited long enough. She deserves that certain someone/couple or a family who will help her feel safe, wanted, and cherished.

Rose is located in Cyprus and, if adopted in the UK, will travel with a passport and has been tested for infectious diseases. She is fully vaccinated and spayed.

name: Kira
description:
This is Kira — a beautiful girl with a glossy, shiny coat. She was found as a stray in Cyprus and has been at a shelter ever since.

Kira is a large female dog who is a confident girl. Kira is super friendly and loving with people she knows and strangers alike. She gets on well with children but we would recommend any children in the home to be aged 10+ due to her size.

Kira enjoys the company of male dogs of a similar size to her. She can be picky with female dogs, but only if they are reactive with her. We also don’t recommend that she is homed with small dogs due to her size.

She is a beautifully well rounded girl who is quite easy going and just happy to be in your company. She takes treats calmly and gently and we suspect she will be a joy to train once you have formed a bond with her. Kira already walks well on the leash.

Kira is healthy, ready, and waiting for someone who sees the incredible companion she can be. She thrives with leadership and will reward the right person or family with loyalty, protection, and deep affection.

Kira will need an experienced handler who understands strong breeds and can continue guiding her with structure, consistency, and love.

Kira is located in Cyprus and, if adopted in the UK, will travel with a passport and has been tested for infectious diseases. She is fully vaccinated and spayed.

name: Sadie
description:
Sadie is a five-year-old female Lurcher who sadly found herself in rescue and, after a month with us for assessment, is now looking for a new home.

Sadie was initially picked up as a stray and was adopted into a home in 2022, where she remained until a change in circumstances meant she found herself back in rescue and due to be put to sleep.

Due to this, despite initially seeming friendly and confident, she will need time to settle into a new home and build trust in her new owners.

Sadie can experience some separation anxiety, which causes her to be destructive at times. She also needs some TLC to continue gaining the weight and muscle she has lost due to stress.

Sadie has proven to be good with other dogs but cannot be rehomed with cats. Sadie would enjoy a quieter life, preferably as an only dog, although this is not a deal breaker.

Sadie has proven to be social and friendly towards everyone she meets. She has enjoyed a pub visit, lots of countryside walks, a good bed and plenty of snacks.

Sadie is crate trained, house trained and well mannered on and off lead. She loves to play fetch, chew on a good bone and is incredibly affectionate, always by your side.

Sadie would make a lovely addition to any home and, of course, as with all my dogs, she will have RBU for life and behavioural support.

She is spayed, microchipped and crate and house trained.

name: Damian
description:
Introducing Damian, a nearly two-year-old male Cross-Breed who weighs 11.4 kg and is ready to steal your heart. Playful, affectionate and full of energy, this boy has a bright, joyful personality and is sure to bring happiness into any home.

Damian adores his toys just as much as he enjoys the company of other dogs. He absolutely loves all the attention and affection he gets from people.

He can be rehomed with female dogs. He can live with a resident dog or as an only dog.

Still young and eager to learn, Damian is ready to find his forever home, a place where he can thrive and share his cheerful spirit every single day. A home where he will be loved and cared for the way he deserves to be.

Could you be the one to make Damian’s dream come true?

Foster with a view to adopt is also an option.

Damian is currently in Cyprus looking for a home in the UK. He will be neutered, vaccinated, microchipped, treated for parasites, have his own pet passport and rescue back-up from Saving Souls Animal Rescue.

name: Ralphie
description:
Ralphie is a 13 month old cavapoo that weighs 10.4kg

Ralphie needs a SPECIAL HOME and isn’t an easy first time pet however he has so much love to give and will make a great companion in the right home with the right training.

Ralphie is super affectionate and has a heart full of love to give, due to his massive heart he can then become very attached to one person and this comes out in separation anxiety with the fear of being left.

Because of this Ralphie needs a home where he can either go to work with his new owner or someone that is indoors and can work on his separation anxiety over time.

Initially Ralphie was a little wary of men but overtime he has grown in confidence and is now happy to enjoy attention from the men in his life- when moving to a new home this may take him a few weeks to settle.

Ralphie knows and listens to commands such as sit, paw, cuddles and kisses ect and is super keen to learn new commands – he will learn and listen to anything for a food reward!

He is toilet trained, plays lovely with toys and enjoys walks. On walks ralphie will happily meet other dogs on the lead however he can pick and choose what dogs he likes and does not like other pets in his home.

For this reason Ralphie will need a PET FREE HOME.

Ralphie doesn’t like loud noises such as crying babies, children playing to loudly or sudden noises so for this reason he would suit a home with no children.

Ralphie is the perfect dog in so many ways but due to his hard start in life he also comes with his own past that sometimes takes over and he has to be reminded that everything is going to be ok.

If you feel that you could provide a second start for ralphie in a suitable environment then please email info@safehavenanimalrescue.co.uk for an application.

name: Delia
description:
Delia is a 2-year-old female Spanish Mastin Cross, with clear sighthound traits in her appearance and behaviour. She is looking for a forever home where she can continue to build her confidence and trust.

When she was first rescued, Delia was extremely shy and fearful, struggling to adjust to her new surroundings. However, thanks to the patience and care of her foster home, she has made remarkable progress.

Now, Delia is much more relaxed and even seeks out affection from those she trusts. She enjoys cuddles and is beginning to show her loving and gentle personality. When out on walks, she is happy to meet new people and other dogs, showing how far she has come in her journey. Her ability to adapt and grow is truly heartwarming.

She gets along very well with other dogs and would benefit from having a calm and confident canine companion in her new home. A steady presence would help her continue to blossom and discover the world at her own pace. Delia is also great with cats, making her a versatile addition to a multi-pet household.

As a sensitive and affectionate soul, Delia deserves a family that will provide her with love, patience, and security. She is currently in Spain but is ready to travel to the UK for adoption. With the right home, she will thrive and form a deep bond with her new family.

If you are interested in giving Delia the loving home she deserves, please reach out to learn more about her and see additional videos.

name: Toby
description:
Toby is a 3-year-old male Cross-Breed who is an extremely friendly and gentle boy.

This gorgeous dog weighs around 40 kg and stands approximately 65 cm tall.

Toby has a loving nature and adores people, making him a wonderful companion.

He is neutered, vaccinated, and microchipped, and also comes with a lifetime RBU (Return to Base) offer, ensuring support throughout his life.

Toby is ready to find a loving home where he can continue to share his affectionate personality and enjoy a fulfilling life.

name: Teddy
description:
Teddy is a medium Basque Shepherd cross puppy, 5 months old.

Teddy is a very handsome puppy who was one of six born from an unplanned litter. Both of his parents are Basque Shepherd mixes, a breed commonly found in the region of Spain where the shelters we work with are based.

All six puppies were originally adopted in Spain, but sadly, Teddy is now looking for a new home through one of the shelters we work closely with.

As an adult, Teddy is expected to be medium-sized. Basque Shepherds are known for being intelligent and active, so he will likely enjoy having plenty to keep his mind and body busy.

Teddy could potentially live with other dogs and may also be able to live with cats following slow, careful introductions. He could equally be happy as the only dog in the home.

He is sociable with children and would make a lovely companion for an active family who enjoys spending time outdoors and including their dog in everyday life.

name: Jerry
description:
Jerry is a 3.5 year old male large terrier cross, currently in kennels in Humberside.

Jerry is a sensitive and complex soul with a big heart, seeking an experienced owner who can provide the structure and love he deserves.

Sadly, Jerry’s life has not been smooth since arriving in the UK, spending much of his time in kennels.

He loves calm people and enjoys walking, playing, and exploring, though he gets stressed in new situations.

Jerry thrives in a rural environment and is clean in his kennel.

This loyal boy needs a semi-rural or countryside home without children or small animals.

He is unsure of cyclists but loves his food and would benefit from ongoing training and support to help him feel safe and loved.

name: Lucky
description:
Lucky is an 18-month-old female Cross-Breed.

Lucky is a medium-sized, friendly dog who has spent most of her life in a foster shelter in Romania.

She stands about 49 cm tall and is known for her sociable nature.

Lucky is comfortable around other dogs, as she currently shares a kennel with them and could potentially live with another dog in her new home.

She is neutered, fully vaccinated, microchipped, and has her own pet passport.

Lucky will be delivered directly to her new adopter after completing the necessary admin checks.

We offer lifetime rescue back-up for all our dogs, ensuring ongoing support for both the dog and their new family.

name: Meg
description:
She is one of two siblings who are currently awaiting their forever homes.

Despite her age, Meg is still a young and vibrant dog who has been waiting for a year without any interest from potential adopters.

Meg is known for her friendly and approachable nature.

She has been neutered, ensuring she won’t contribute to overpopulation. Meg is microchipped, which helps in identifying her should she ever get lost.

She is fully vaccinated, providing her with protection against common canine diseases.

Additionally, she has been tested for Brucellosis and other relevant conditions, ensuring her health status is well-documented.

Although Meg has not yet found her forever home, she remains hopeful and ready to bring joy and companionship to a new family.

If you are looking for a loving and well-cared-for dog, Meg might be the perfect addition to your home.

name: Sam
description:
Sam is a 9 to 10 year old male Cross-Breed, looking for his retirement home!

He is a small Cross-Breed dog and a handsome chap.

He is waiting in foster in Kings Lynn, Norfolk and on reservation, he would be brought over directly to his new owner’s home.

Sam is a little shy at first and is a bit wary of men, but with time and love, he would be fine.

He would suit a couple or individual, possibly retired.

He deserves to spend the rest of his life in his forever home with lots of love.

We are told that he is about 9 or 10, but he looks younger.

Please consider this gorgeous boy. We provide lifetime RBU.

name: Angel
description:
Angel is a 3-year-old female Cross-Breed. She exudes a charming and friendly demeanour, often engaging in playful antics that highlight her affectionate nature.

Her gentle personality and warmth make her a lovely companion, whether during playtime or quiet moments at home.

Angel’s playful side is balanced by her calm and loving temperament, making her well-suited for a variety of households.

Having been neutered, fully vaccinated, and microchipped, Angel is in excellent health and ready for her forever home.

Her responsible care has ensured that she’s in great condition, both physically and emotionally. Weighing 26 kg and standing at around 50 cm tall, she is a moderately sized dog, reflecting her mixed-breed heritage.

Her size makes her adaptable to different living environments, whether in a larger house or a cosy home.

Angel’s endearing personality extends to her social interactions with other dogs.

She gets along well with them, showing her ability to fit in with a multi-dog household. Her friendly and approachable nature is sure to make her a delightful addition to any family.

name: Cerys
description:
Cerys is a 5-month-old female cross breed dog who was discovered alongside two other female pups abandoned on the roadside in Romania.

Currently, she is under the care of an English lady living in Romania. She is described as a smallish mixed breed dog and has been socialized with larger resident dogs, exhibiting good compatibility with them.

Cerys has completed her vaccination regimen and has been microchipped, in addition to undergoing all the necessary blood tests to meet DEFRA regulations for dogs originating from other countries.

It’s anticipated that she will grow into a small to medium-sized adult dog, weighing approximately 15 kg to 18 kg.

Cerys is adaptable to various living situations, suitable for a family, a couple, or an individual, and she has a laid-back demeanor for her age.

While she would appreciate having a canine companion, it’s not an essential requirement for her. Although she hasn’t been tested with cats yet, there’s a possibility of conducting such a test before her relocation.

Full rescue support is provided for all dogs, including Cerys, when necessary.

She eagerly awaits the opportunity for a fresh start in the UK and would thrive in a loving home environment. Her sisters Inca and Holly are also seeking new homes.

name: Minnie
description:
Minnie is a 10 month old female Cross-Breed puppy, playful and trusting, yet sadly overlooked. She is small-medium in size, weighing 16 kg and standing at 50-51 cm, perfect for a knee-height companion.

MINNIE was originally found near the road, her mum was hit by the car and didn’t survive. She was a tiny puppy and had no chance to survive if volunteers in Belarus would not rescue her.

She went to a Foster family together with her brother Alex. Alex was happily Adopted in UK. Minnie arrived in UK in June , and still dreams about her forever home.

MINNIE is at Foster now, with other dogs and older kids. And this is what they say:

” What a joy it’s been to train such a smart and eager pup like Minnie! In just 3 weeks at our foster home, she’s made remarkable improvement in impulse control, obedience, and even tried her paw at agility exercises with so much excitement. Can you believe how far she’s come in such a short time?Previously, we mentioned some of her challenges, but let’s see how she’s improved:

“Can be unsure around pushchairs.” Not anymore! Minnie is now completely calm around pushchairs, whether they’re coming toward her, walking beside her, or passing by. She’s unbothered and confident.

“May bark or chew on your shoes sometimes.” While Minnie still loves to carry shoes around the house, we’re working on giving her a more appropriate comfort object. It seems to be a part of her young age, but she’s already shifting her focus to healthier chew options like bones, Kongs, or long-lasting treats like dried ears and tails.

Minnie’s even turned it into a game—she loves tossing treats in the air and chasing them around the house. And the best part? No more barking at home! When she first arrived, she was quite demanding, but now she patiently waits for her meals, even with our two other dogs around.

She’s grown more confident and no longer feels the need to follow us like a shadow. While we haven’t left her alone at home yet, she’s happy to stay in a room by herself as long as the door is open.

“Reactive on walks.” Minnie can be reactive if we’re not fully focused on her, but we lovingly call her our “mindfulness trainer” for this reason. When we stay engaged—by changing pace, asking her to come, throwing treats for her to find—she’s fantastic.

No distractions from birds, squirrels, or even people. It’s only when we get distracted ourselves that some of her reactivity returns, so with the right attention, Minnie is a joy to walk!

“Sometimes unsure around kids or female dogs.” Minnie is improving here, too. She’s now playful with most dogs, regardless of their size or gender.

When it comes to children, she can still be a bit reactive, especially when they approach her too quickly, but with patience and positive reinforcement, she’s getting better.

MINNIE is adorable pup, too young to be perfect in everything. She is can be nervous and shy at start but she is very friendly and playful. She is very loving, very curious and smart.

MINNIE can be unsure of young kids,  but she loves older kids 13+. She will perfectly suit home with the other friendly and confident  large or medium male dog as really enjoy canine company

MINNIE has no known health issues; not spayed (arrived 5 months ago at early age, rescue will contribute to costs). Full vaccination pack, provided worms treatment, microchipped. Brucella C. tested.

name: Poppy
description:
Poppy is a 7-year-old female Cross-Breed. She was abandoned in the woods of Romania alongside another mother and eleven puppies.

Sadly, only six of the puppies survived and have since been adopted, but Poppy has remained in the shelter for two and a half years, patiently waiting for her forever home.

She is a shy but loving girl whose entire demeanour brightens when she receives human attention.

With gentle care, she blossoms into an affectionate and grateful companion. She gets along well with other dogs and cats, making her a great addition to a multi-pet household.

Poppy walks well on the lead, though she will need time to adjust and may benefit from some further training. At around 35 kg and 50 cm tall, she is a medium-sized dog with a gentle presence.

She has been spayed and is fully vaccinated, ensuring she is ready for a fresh start in a loving home.

After waiting so long, Poppy deserves a family that will cherish her. She is looking for a patient and understanding owner who will help her settle into home life.

Could you be the one to offer her the home of her dreams? Full rescue backup (RBU) is provided.

name: Orla
description:
Orla is a ten year old female German Wirehaired Pointer. Orla is a truly gorgeous dog, inside and out.

Like so many older dogs given up to the shelter when they are no longer useful for hunting, Orla has a wonderful nature, calm and kind.

She seems amazingly well balanced given her background. She is confident and friendly around the kennels, getting on well with all the other dogs.

WIth people she is very attached and affectionate, not showing much fear. She walks well on the lead so far (that could change on an exciting walk) and she is calm in the car.

She loves her food, and now just needs a cosy home with some good company to make her retirement dreams come true.

Orla will be an amazing companion dog in the right home.

If you are interested in giving wonderful Orla a home, she is available at Setter Brittany Pointer Rescue. Orla is in Spain and is ready to travel to her forever home in the UK.

name: Victor
description:
Victor is a 3 year old large male German Shepherd Cross, standing 55cm from shoulder to floor, currently at the Nicosia sanctuary.

Gentle is the word all visitors use to describe this handsome boy. After being rescued, Victor spent over three years in private kennels under the care of his rescuer. Once space became available, he joined the sanctuary to ensure he finds his happy ever after.

Victor is an absolute sweetheart! He’s affectionate and loves cuddles, even with people he’s just met.

While he has been walked alongside Athena (one of the resident dogs) and ignored her, he’d likely be happiest as an only dog.

He enjoys playing, running for toys, and a good game of tug. Victor walks well on a lead and is happy to join you for a run. He’s clever and loves training, especially if treats are involved!

Victor could join a home with dog-savvy children. He’s a gorgeous, affectionate boy who is sure to make a wonderful companion.

SPDC adoption package and home checks apply.

name: Rina
description:
Rina is a 7-year-old female Cross-Breed. She is a gentle, calm dog with a heart full of gold who has spent much of her life waiting for someone to notice her.

After enduring years in a harsh shelter, she has learned patience and resilience, quietly surviving without demanding attention.

Since coming to Azil Danica in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Rina has slowly begun to bloom, revealing her kind and affectionate nature.

She walks well on a lead and enjoys the company of other dogs, showing her social and adaptable personality. Although she ignores cats, her calm temperament makes her a perfect companion for a peaceful household.

Rina thrives in environments where she can relax and enjoy gentle interactions, always eager to be part of a loving family.

Despite her quiet past, she now expresses her affection openly, forming bonds with humans and other dogs alike. Rina is vaccinated, microchipped, spayed, and treated for fleas and worms, making her ready for adoption.

She would do best in a home that appreciates a calm, gentle dog who loves companionship but doesn’t demand constant attention. After years of waiting, she is ready to finally experience the joy of a forever home.

name: Luna
description:
Luna is a 4-year-old female Cross-Breed. She is a calm and gentle dog with an endlessly kind nature, who has shown incredible strength and devotion throughout her life.

Once abandoned in the middle of a busy city, she was courageously guarding her seven newborn puppies, showing her protective instincts and maternal heart.

After being rescued and brought to Azil Danica in Bosnia, Luna watched her puppies find their forever homes, patiently waiting for the day she would get hers.

Despite her quiet wait, Luna never lost her optimism and continues to greet everyone who passes her kennel with a wagging tail. She walks beautifully on a lead and adores people, always showing affection and social grace.

Luna also gets along well with other dogs, demonstrating her friendly and adaptable personality in a shelter environment.

Her ideal home would be one that recognises her gentle, loving nature and offers her the companionship and stability she has been patiently waiting for.

Vaccinated, spayed, microchipped, and treated for fleas and worms, Luna is healthy and ready for adoption.

She is calm, social, and eager to form a deep bond with her future family, making her a perfect companion for someone who wants a loving, devoted dog.

After all she has given and endured, Luna truly deserves a home filled with love and care.

name: Maya
description:
Maya is a 4-year-old female Cross-Breed. She is spayed, fully vaccinated, and currently living in a private shelter in Romania.

Maya and her siblings were rescued as young puppies, and despite her early hardships, she has blossomed into a sweet and affectionate girl who loves both canine and human company.

She shares her kennel with her sister, Evie, and the two have grown up side by side. Having spent her life surrounded by other dogs, Maya feels most at ease when she has doggy companions around her.

She would likely enjoy joining a home with another friendly dog, though she could also adapt well to being an only dog if her new family provides her with plenty of love and attention.

Maya’s biggest wish is simple — to finally have a family of her own who will give her the affection, patience, and stability she deserves. She’s a gentle, loyal soul who would make a loving addition to the right home.

The rescue ensures a full home check, adoption donation, and lifetime backup and support to help Maya transition smoothly into her forever home.

name: Penny
description:
Meet the sweet and affectionate Penny. Penny is a two year old female Collie Cross, large in size, who is loving and playful once she gains trust.

Penny is such a sweet girl once she gains trust. She is a bit nervous but loves cuddles and playing. If her trusted staff member took her to the paddock, Penny would run around with them and really enjoy herself.

She is great on the lead and doesn’t pull. Penny hasn’t encountered children on walks but has been fine walking past dogs and people. She handles passing cars well, and even a tractor went past with no reaction.

She has growled at dogs in the kennels, but with slow introductions and trust-building, this can likely be managed. She doesn’t like getting into cars much and had to be lifted in to travel.

Her new owners will need to understand she needs time to get to know people.

Penny’s new home will ideally be familiar with herding breeds or understand their traits. She will need boundaries to minimize any guarding behaviour and should be kept busy with puzzle toys or jobs to occupy her.

Penny will need plenty of exercise, though this should be on lead or long line until she has reliable recall. She suffers from motion sickness in cars, which can be treated with medication.

She needs to learn to trust people at her own pace. Any males in the household should understand she is wary of men, and this trust may take longer to develop.

Penny was toilet trained and used a crate to sleep with the door open in her previous home, although she is not fully crate trained.

She may need a refresher in a new home. She has previously guarded food, so she should be fed in her safe space until this behaviour has ceased.

Penny will need someone around most of the day to gradually build her alone time and spend quality time with her to build trust.

Penny is a lovely, cuddly, playful girl who needs boundaries, patience, kindness, and time.

She needs to be kept busy to allow her natural behaviours to be met and given time to know she is safe and can trust her new family so that she can relax and flourish.

name: Vera
description:
Meet the energetic and intelligent Vera. Vera is a two year old female Malinois Cross, medium/large in size, who is very nervous at first but settles to become friendly once she trusts people.

Vera is very nervous of people when she first meets them. She can sometimes nip when overexcited or when taking treats, so her new family will need to continue working on this with her.

Vera accepts a collar, harness, and lead, though she can be excitable on the lead and tends to pull, especially at the start of walks.

She has shown some reactivity toward other dogs and people while on walks but is generally good with dogs she knows, though she may growl if they come too close.

Vera will need a very active family due to her high energy level and breed traits, with lots of long walks and mental stimulation through training.

Vera can have poo accidents in her kennel, so her new home will need to work on toilet training.

She previously suffered from severe separation anxiety, including when left alone in a separate room while her family was still present, causing barking and yelping.

She has managed to be left for up to four hours with another dog but still shows signs of separation anxiety in kennels.

Vera has never shown food aggression, but she is known to counter-surf and steal food lying around, including other dogs’ food. She will need continued training and should be fed separately from other dogs.

name: Bob and Charlie
description:
Bob and Charlie are 5years old and a bonded pair male Podenco cross.

We have the sad story of Bob and Charlie, who are 5 and a half year old Podenco mix brothers. They have the traditional, tan, short coats and they are gentle lads, with big hearts and very kind natures.

They are a little chunky atm, but we think that’s a reflection of how much they have been loved and how contented they are.

They love all people, no matter the age, and small kids will have their face licked off if the dogs can reach. They do not jump up, but will certainly welcome you and be happy to meet you.

As big as they are, they think they are lap dogs. At night, they love their owners so much, that they both like to sleep in their bedroom to be close.

The very sad part is that the boys owner just died, and their mum will have to downsize and maybe to a flat. She doesn’t want to let them go but she can’t see how she will cope and is looking for a home, if possible for both to remain together.

They have only known themselves for the last 5 and half years and we are looking for one owner for both, but I’m sure they wouldn’t mind being split if it meant not having to go into a shelter.

So to start, let’s just look for one new mum and dad and see how that goes!

There is a lot of information we need to get for them – ie how tall? Weight, But for now lets get them out there to show you all.

Charlie is more dominant, he looks after his brother. he does like his love, especially his shoulders being massaged, but not as much as Bob. Bob could be tickled all day long, even to pulling your hand to keep stroking him when you stop.

They will sit watching while you eat, but they do not beg. If you open a biscuit tin or packet of cheese, does not matter where they are, they will smell or hear it.

Their senses are amazing! They can be left for a few hours, they will just sleep and I have had no complaints of any barking when i leave the house, the neighbours know when i arrive home though, they bark to greet.

They are good guard dogs, they only bark if there is a knock on the door or if someone is passing, but they are only saying hello we are here there is not a dangerous bone in their body.

They are good with other dogs, they used to have a little play mate, she ran them ragged. Although cats they would chase out of the garden.

They do need training on the lead, due to circumstances they have not been walked enough and not for a long time either. Bob will settle on the lead but Charlie tends to pull a lot and he is very strong, but I expect a halti will sort that.

They get excited in the car. Bob is very scared at the vets. Charlie has no problem. They have their passports Overall they are very laid back and relaxed dogs and will be sorry to see them leave.

name: Miracle
description:
Miracle is a 2-year-old female Cross-Breed. She’s a gentle soul who starts off shy but quickly transforms into a deeply loyal companion once she feels safe. Her soft nature shines brightest in quiet spaces where she can build trust at her own pace.

Miracle is loving, affectionate, and happiest when she gets calm company and steady reassurance. She travels beautifully in the car and greets strangers with a friendly attitude, though she still appreciates being given room to settle.

Her housetraining and lovely manners make her easy to have around.

On walks, Miracle is polite on the lead but can show reactivity towards some dogs, usually due to excitement or frustration.

Continued socialisation will help her feel more relaxed in those moments. She has previously lived with a male dog and could again if their personalities suit.

She has also lived with a cat, but her food guarding means she may be better in a cat-free home or one that can manage feeding routines carefully.

Miracle has recovered from a past leg injury and toe surgery, and although she still enjoys her walks, she benefits from a home that understands her physical limits.

At her core, Miracle is thoughtful, loyal, and eager for a peaceful environment where she can fully flourish with patient people by her side.

name: Lenny
description:
Lenny is a 4-year-old small sized American Bulldog cross.

Lenny is currently in our kennels in Wrexham, North Wales.

Lenny is a 4-year-old American Bulldog cross with a sweet and gentle nature. Although a little unsure when meeting new people, once he feels safe, he blossoms into a playful, affectionate boy who loves nothing more than a good toy session!

If you are happy to throw a squeaky toy for him all day long then you will very quickly make a new best friend. He really is a gem with so much potential.

Lenny is crate trained and finds comfort in having a safe space of his own. He’s also house trained and keeps his environment clean, making him a joy to have around the home.

He travels well in the car, making him a great buddy for road trips or vet visits without the stress, in fact he seems to get more excited about being In the car than the actual walk!

He’s shown himself to be neutral and polite with other dogs when out and about on a walk, and seems disinterested in cats, but would be best as the only pet in the home,

Lenny can be a little pushy in certain situations, particularly when asked to do something he’s unsure about – a trait that’s not unusual for his breed.

Because of this, a confident, calm owner would really help him thrive. Previous experience with American Bulldogs or similar breeds would be helpful, though it isn’t essential.

He would benefit from multiple meet & greets to help build a strong bond before going home, and he’s currently available for either adoption or temporary foster.

With all the change he’s experienced lately, he’s bound to be a little confused and would really flourish in a stable, loving environment where he can feel safe and settled again.

Lenny is neutered, vaccinated, flea and wormed.

A link to our adoption process can be found below:

Once we have received your application this will be reviewed by our dog team and if you are a suitable match one of our volunteers will be in touch within 7 days to discuss your application in more detail.

You will then be invited to meet the dog, and we encourage 2-3 meet & greets for you to get to know your chosen dog, we are happy to introduce you to multiple dogs on the day of they are suitable matches.

We do request all household members attend meet & greets including resident dogs.

If successful we will request a home check at this stage along with proof of identification and address. We will require written permission from a landlord for all applicants in rented accommodation.

Please note we require all resident dogs to be neutered and up to date with vaccinations before we will proceed with the adoption.

attributes.Breed: Year- belgian malinois cross american bulldog

name: Bear is a male 2
description:
Bear is a 2-year-old Belgian Malinois Cross American bulldog

Bear is currently in our kennels in Wrexham, North Wales

Bear, our 2-year-old heartbreaker, struts his stuff on the leash like a pro, gives paw like a true gentleman, and even tucks himself in at night!

We suspect he’s part Malinois, part bull breed, and all mischief. Sure, he can jump a 6ft obstacle and redecorate with the best of them, but hey, who doesn’t love a bit of chaos?

Bear’s health is top-notch, and his intelligence is off the chats—now if only we could convince him to use it for good!

Bear is fine with other dogs when out and about but we would not rehome him with another dog in the home. He will benefit from still being socialised with other dogs outside the home.

He is best suited to a home with older children only, where he can enjoy structure, calm, and consistency.

Someone with breed experience is important as Bear is a high energy dog who is very intelligent – his new owner will need to be able to give him enough physical and mental stimulation and in reward you will have an amazing dog!

Bear is house trained, crate trained and good with everyone he meets

A link to our adoption process can be found below:
